Client stays derived from rows, because nothing publishes a client directory.

**Opening a matter is one screen that grows instead of squeezing.** It fits its content first and caps
at the viewport second, and when it caps only the body moves — the header and the action bar hold, so
a refusal can never scroll out from under the hand reaching for it. Matter information and people sit
on the left across two tabs; the client and the conflict check stand together on the right, permanently
in view, because they are the same question.

Status replaces the old framing and reads Prospective, Active and Closed.

**Practice area is a dropdown that seeds itself.** The firm's own matter types existed as an API and
nothing ever seeded them, so a new firm met an empty field. Twenty starting areas are offered
alongside whatever the firm has already adopted; choosing one creates the firm's own type in that
moment, editable from then on, and hands it straight to the docket so the column and its filter know
about it at once.

**One correction could not land, and is rendered rather than dropped.** The create operation accepts
only Prospective or Active, so Closed stands in the list disabled, marked, naming exactly what it
waits on. Creating a matter already closed needs the contract widened.

The middle status is stored as `open` and printed as "Active" — a wire code is not a word anybody
reads. The two meet in one file and nowhere else.
- **Where a modal panel sits on the screen is now one module, and it keeps every panel off the screen's edges.** `styles/recipes/modal-stage.css` holds every placement rule: `mc-modal-stage`, the viewport pulled in by the new `size.modal-gutter` token (32px), centring its panel with flex and capping it there by flex shrinking; and `mc-modal-panel`, what makes any panel its child, so the panel recipes keep only their look and carry no `max-h-*` utility any more. `internal/modal-stage.svelte` is the stage's one piece of markup, rendered by `Dialog.Content` and `AlertDialog.Content`. `internal/modal-placement.ts` is the closed placement axis (`centered | anchored`), stamped on every panel and taken by `Dialog.Content` as `placement`; the command palette says `anchored` instead of reaching for a utility. `modal-geometry/` is the diagnostic: a Playwright sweep that measures every modal specimen at every screen size in its matrix, screenshots it, and fails an edge nearer than the gutter. Pinned in `test/modal-stage.test.ts` and `test/modal-geometry.test.ts`; ruled in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.
- **A panel's second line is the record it is acting on, by the number somebody quotes.** The subtitle slot on `ActionDialog` and `RecordWindow` was contracted to name what is being acted on and to carry the record's own reference, and the owner ruled on 2026-09-08 that it is not the place for a paragraph about what a subsystem is for. Nothing enforced either, and the slot was typed `string`.

**A slot typed `string` accepts a paragraph.** Across 82 panel openings, 18 of 54 subtitles were prose about the subsystem, four billing panels put a number and a sentence in one interpolated string behind a middle dot in three places and an em dash in a fourth, `tabular-nums` was hand written 138 times, and the preview-before-save the owner asked for had reached exactly one file.

**So the slot takes a `RecordSubject` and the design system renders it.** An optional `RecordReference` — `kind`, `number`, and a `standing` of `drawn`, `tentative` or `preview` — plus short facts about that subject. The three standings are the domain's own: a matter number is drawn, a consultation number is tentative and outlives the matter opening, and a preview is what the next record would take. `RecordSubjectLine` states the preview's own wording in one place instead of one file, renders "A number is drawn when this is saved." rather than silence where no number exists yet, and owns the separator so no call site chooses one. The bare `string` arm is gone, which is the mechanism rather than a side effect: a sentence about the act has nowhere left to go, because the heading names the act.

Every panel that carried prose lost it — deleted where it restated the heading, moved beside the field it explains where it was load-bearing. Panels that held a record's number and showed something else now show the number: the two queue acts on a call or text state that message's own reference, the three custodian panels state the packet's custody number, and bill review states the invoice number.
- **A capability could read `not-started` in the build register while sixteen modules, twelve routes
and a registered close gate stood behind it, and nothing could see the contradiction. Two more rules
in the ledger-staleness scan close that, and four nodes in the register were wrong because of it.**

**Why nothing saw it.** Every rule in `tooling/lint-ledger-staleness/` keys on a node **naming a
path**: it resolves the path, asks whether some other node accounts for it, asks whether the sentence
around it claims the path is absent. A node that describes its own absence in prose gives those rules
nothing to hold. `financial.trust.reconciliation`'s evidence was "in slice 3-2 scope … no code" and
named no path at all; `financial.trust.close-rule` named the hook file, which exists and which the
matters node correctly accounts for, and made its absence claim about a symbol rather than a path.
Both were silent by construction, and both sat at `not-started` over `packages/trust`'s
reconciliation, matching, statement-import and three-way-proof modules, over
`apps/api-worker/src/routes/trust-reconciliation.ts`, and over a close precondition registered in the
matter composition root and tested at two layers.

**The new rule reads no prose.** A node carries `slices:`; a `status.d/<slug>.md` fragment carries
`built:`. A `not-started` node whose slice fragments all report `built: in-progress` or `built: done`,
and one of whose **siblings** is already shipped under that same slice, is two committed documents
contradicting each other — no filesystem, no keyword matching, no guessing at English.

**The narrowing is the whole design, and it was measured rather than assumed.** The unnarrowed form
fires 19 times and 14 of those are one correct idiom: a capability tagged to the slice that built the
_substrate it will reuse_. `payments.port` sits on the port system, every `portal.capabilities.*` on
the document slice whose engine it will call. What separates those from a stale node is where the
stream's output landed — their substrate is in another subtree, while a stream that has already
shipped this node's own siblings is demonstrably working inside this one. Restricting to
`not-started` drops two more: `designed` and `planned` are **attested** pre-code states, where a spec
or a plan was written and somebody recorded that the build had not begun, and widening to them buys
one true positive at the price of one false. Final measurement: **2 hits, both real, no exemptions**.
A second rule holds the input honest — a `slices:` entry naming no fragment would silently switch the
first rule off, and 267 tags across 235 nodes all resolve today.

**What the register was saying, and what it says now.** Reconciliation is `partial`, not
`not-started`: the whole workflow — a recorded bank period, an import that previews before it stores,
ranked match candidates a person confirms, and a three-way proof frozen on close — is on main behind
routes, with no screen on any of it. The zero-balance close precondition is `shipped`; its "all bills
paid" half is deliberately not registered, because an uncollectable receivable's lawful exit is a
write-off. Two further nodes the narrowing surfaced were verified by hand and corrected the same way:
per-account jurisdiction binding and location-on-trust-accounts are both `partial`, both shipping
their binding and their refusals while nothing yet resolves a rule profile through the port.

Shipped moves 244 → 245 and partial 186 → 189, so shipped-plus-partial goes 430 → 434 of 705, 61% to
62%. Four capabilities that existed were being counted as work not begun.
- Matter notes: edit and delete replace correction-by-revision and withdrawal, a note records when the thing it describes happened, and a note can point at the matter's documents.

Three changes on the owner's direction, hours after the note primitive first shipped.

**The model collapses to one row.** The first cut held an identity row plus a chain of revisions, with three `RAISE(ABORT)` triggers making a stored body unrewritable and withdrawal as a state rather than a delete. An edit now overwrites and a delete removes the row. The owner's reason: replacing a note with another note every time somebody fixes a word accumulates without end. What it costs is stated rather than buried — there is no record of what a note said before, and nothing survives a deletion but an audit row carrying identifiers — and the superseded reasoning is kept in `docs/decisions/pending/` rather than deleted, because the position was really taken. The migration is a reviewed rebuild that carries every standing note across with its current text; `notes:retract` retires and deleting rides `notes:write`.

**A note carries two times and stops conflating them.** `created_at` is when somebody typed it; the new `occurred_on` / `occurred_at_time` / `time_zone` are when the thing it describes happened, on the calendar's model — a civil date, an optional wall clock, and a zone required whenever there is a clock. Every read orders by the occurrence falling back to the written day, and so does the federated timeline source, whose `timeColumnShape` moves from `instant` to `civilDate`. That puts a note about Tuesday's call beside Tuesday's hearing, which is how `matterEvent`, `matterDeadline` and `timeEntry` are already ordered; the one source that orders by when the row was written is the audit log, and that is named as its weakness rather than copied.

**A note can point at the matter's documents.** `matter_note_document` is a many-to-many link on the `matter_asset_document` model, and it links a handle rather than moving bytes: upload stays the File Manager's presigned-upload and quarantine chokepoint, so an attached document keeps its versions, its holds and its reachability from discovery. Deleting a note detaches its documents and deletes none of them. The merge-field fitness function now refuses the link table too, since a resolver reaching it would be one join from the bodies of every note discussing the document being assembled.

The composer shows every field the note will carry before anything is typed, generated ones included: the matter, the writer's name and the instant it will be stamped with.
- Matter notes: a note is written, read, changed and deleted in the shared record window, its date and time sit on one line, and a document can be attached before the note exists.

The owner's first review round on the section, and one report that did not reproduce.

**The composer is gone; the record window took its place.** Writing a note was a form that unfolded inside the list it would join — a second place to learn where a note's fields live, and a list that lost its own shape while somebody was typing. A note now opens in the same two-pane window a time entry and a cost open in: the record on the left, its Attachments tab on the right, one action bar underneath. Creating one is that window with nothing in it and its fields already open, which is what makes starting a note a modal act rather than an inline one. The primary action reads **New Note**, the occurrence field is labelled **Date** with **Time** beside it on the same line, and the shared window brings a printable sheet with it — a note states both of the times it carries, so a reader years later can see how long after the call it was written down.

**A document is attached while the note is still a draft.** The picker offers the matter's own files from the first keystroke; the choices are held in the window and written the moment the note is. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is copied, exactly as before. Where a note is written but one of its documents does not attach, the list says which one and why rather than reporting a failure to save — the note exists, and somebody told otherwise would write it twice. Notes have no upload path of their own, so the shared attachments tab now withholds its dropzone from any record that cannot take one, rather than rendering a control that swallows a file in silence.

**On the report that the section never stopped loading:** it did not reproduce. The section was driven end to end against a real Worker — an empty matter, a matter with notes, a note written through the window, a document attached before saving — and the list settled every time; so does the route's empty-page envelope, now pinned by its own tests. What the rebuild changed is the shape that made a permanent skeleton possible at all. The notes read is an effect of its own, so nothing else the screen wants (who is signed in, the roster, the matter's files) can abort it before the read is even asked for, and a failed read settles the list with a stated reason and a Retry instead of leaving the skeleton standing. A section sitting on a skeleton is indistinguishable from a firm whose record cannot be read, which is why that is now structurally unreachable rather than merely unobserved.

Two things found on the way. A size utility off the generated spacing scale (`w-160`, `w-192`) compiles to no rule at all and no gate says so, which had left a search field and a date field full-bleed where both were meant to be narrow; the trap is recorded in the UI conventions. And `apps/web/e2e/login.spec.ts` no longer matches the shipped sign-in screen — the suite is not wired into CI, so it rotted unnoticed, and one of its assertions now contradicts shipped behaviour rather than merely naming a stale selector.
- **The preview-before-save leaves the call log.** The owner's ruling of 2026-09-08 — where a record carries a reference number a person reads back, the panel states the number the next one would draw while it is still being filled in, and says that it is a preview rather than a reservation — was written generally and reached one file. The call log had the effect, the wording, the racing-reads guard and the reset, hand-written; every other panel that mints a number showed nothing.

`PreviewedNumber` (`@magna-carta/design-system/record-reference`) holds it once. Each domain keeps its own endpoint and its own scope key — a call's number is scoped to the UTC day it happened on, a matter's to the firm's numbering scheme, a packet's to the custody register — and folding those into one route would put every domain's numbering rules in one handler. What is shared is the shape of the answer, the guard against a stale read landing after a newer one, and the words the reader is told: the parts that were drifting. It knows nothing about how the answer is fetched, so the app's transport and failure model stay in the app.

Two creation panels state the honest half now. **New Matter** says which number the save will draw and that it will — a consultation draws its own tentative number, an open matter draws the matter number, and an intake draws neither, because no number of any kind exists before a matter is at least a consultation. **New Packet** previews the custody number, except where the packet was carried in from a paper deeds register, in which case the number already written on its physical label is the packet's real number and the save only records it.
- `ActionDialog` has a fourth kind, `reading`, and the matter-status window is its first caller.

A reading panel states a fact and seats any step it offers beside that fact — Close Matter, Reopen — rather than in the action bar, whose one control says "Close" because nothing was begun. The props are now a discriminated union on `kind`: the acting kinds require a commit exactly as they did, and the reading kind forbids one, so neither arm got weaker to admit the other. The kind table gained a row (`commitVariant: null`) and the bar renders its commit only when there is a variant to render it in.

The status window had merged composing `Dialog.Content` by hand — the shape the `hand-composed-modal` rule refuses — and left `main` red on `lint:one-ui`, because nothing before merge ran the rule. It migrates rather than taking an allowance: it postdates the shell. Two visible changes on that window: "Done" reads "Close", and the control is no longer disabled while a step is in flight, since the shell owns the dismissal.
- **The event participant's role is the product's dropdown-with-add instead of a bare text box.** `apps/web/src/lib/calendar/participant-role-field.svelte` offers `PARTICIPANT_ROLE_OPTIONS` (eighteen roles, alphabetical, in `calendar-vocabulary.ts`) and ends the list in `Combobox.AddOption`, so a role the list has never heard of is still typed and kept — the column stays free text, which the per-firm schema rules deliberately because the vocabulary is jurisdiction-specific and nothing downstream reads it.

The standing rule under _Data entry_ in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md` already decided the control ("a vocabulary that is not closed but is not free either is the product's dropdown-with-add … the same control in every such field"); the location field on the same form and the matter-party role already had it, and this field was the one that had not been carried over. A closed dropdown was considered and rejected: the roles a practice needs do not close, and a fixed list missing one makes somebody pick a wrong-but-adjacent role, which corrupts the consistency the list existed for and does it invisibly.

`settledParticipantRole` collapses a typed role onto an offered spelling in any casing, so "court reporter" no longer founds a second role beside "Court reporter"; anything unlisted is kept exactly as typed, trimmed. The field's name stays "Role" rather than the clearer "Attending as" because `AddOption` reads the name into a row that says `Add <name>`. Pinned by `apps/web/test/calendar-participant-roles.test.ts`.
- **Name prefix and suffix are one control, everywhere a person is named.** `apps/web/src/lib/names/honorific-field.svelte` over `@magna-carta/directory/honorifics` replaces the three plain text boxes on the Directory's person forms (the new-person names section, the record's names pane) and the account profile's seams. It is the product's own combobox with its add row, so the suggestion list is a shortcut and the typing is still the answer.

The lists are SUGGESTIONS over free text and the module header says so twice. `directory_person.prefix` and `.suffix` are unchanged and unvalidated: nothing compares against these arrays, and a closed list here would refuse a person their own name. Ordered by how often a firm meets them rather than alphabetically, with the judicial and legal forms high, because that is what a legal practice writes.

One departure from the categories picker this control is otherwise modelled on: closing the list settles the value on what was TYPED rather than on what was picked. There, an unpicked word would mint a firm-wide category and must be deliberate; here there is nothing to mint, and dropping the text would be the control eating a name.
- **The loading region holds a read's whole state set, states a stall, announces its finish and measures every settle.** `LoadingRegion` gains `failed` with a `failure` snippet (rendered first, whatever else is true, so the failure-exit ruling is structural), `empty` with an `emptyState` snippet, `refreshing` for a re-read that keeps the content on screen while marking the region busy, and `onRetry`. Past fifteen seconds in flight the region says "Still reading …. This is taking longer than it should." above the shape and offers Retry, so a permanent skeleton cannot happen by construction. One status line carries the sentence and then says the read finished. Every settle writes a User Timing measure and dispatches `mc-loading-settled`; the app shell records it as a `loading` breadcrumb, so a report says which reads a member waited on and for how long. The four-branch chain around every region in `apps/web` folds into the region, and the Refresh control and the directory's duplicate check use `refreshing` in place of hand-written busy marks.

**Every fixture's words come from one invented vocabulary.** `@magna-carta/design-system/loading-fixtures` supplies people, organizations, matters, dates, amounts and a sentence by index, plausible in length and provably not a client's; the story, the gallery and every surface draw from it.

**Two more gates.** `silent-loading` fails a null-sentinel branch that renders nothing or a bare "Reading…" sentence, the gap the first rule could not see; `fixture-shape` fails a fixture that renders a component its region's children never do, with `{@render}` expanded to the snippet it names. Both are proved against known-bad input. The developer-console gallery adds the state set, and a fitness test measures the bone's contrast on every surface in every theme and mode (1.16:1 to 1.59:1 today, against a 3:1 non-text target the owner has yet to rule on) and pins a floor under it.

**And the round after it.** A fourth rule, `loading-label`, holds a region's label to the house voice (a capitalised gerund, never "Loading", no terminal punctuation), since the finished and stalled sentences are derived from it. The callers the migration left short now supply what their regions can use: Retry on the conflicts posture panel and the matter search, a failed versions read carried into the file inspector instead of collapsing to "no versions yet", a guard against a second concurrent integrity check, and one announcement per region on the version chip. Every fixture date is on the vocabulary in the shape its column needs. The developer console's performance module lists the reads the tab waited on, from the User Timing measures the regions write.
- **A read that takes a limit now says when it hit it, and six feature-ledger nodes stop claiming work
is underway where only a branch or a document is.** Two unrelated defects, one shape: an instrument
that reads healthy while reporting nothing.

**The calendar's zone read returns its own clamp.** `readOpenDeadlineTimeZones` took a `limit` and
returned a bare array, so no caller could tell a complete zone list from one the bound cut short
except by over-reading and comparing. That is not an under-filled page: the zone list is what the
overdue narrowing derives one cutoff per zone from, so a zone the read never returns contributes no
cutoff, and every deadline recorded in it matches neither the overdue bound nor the due-today
window — a whole jurisdiction goes unreported while every counter beside it reads healthy. The read
now over-reads by one itself and answers `{ timeZones, clamped }`, the shape the notification
digest's window read already uses. `clamped` is a boolean on purpose: over-reading by one learns
_that_ the bound bit and never _by how much_, and a magnitude invented there would be the same
dishonesty one level down.

The notification comparison sweep had hand-rolled exactly this at its call site, correctly, and now
consumes the signal instead. Its `notifications.comparison_zone_discovery_truncated` counter is
unchanged in meaning and value — still one per truncated **pass**, charged to both deadline kinds.
The deadline-list route discards the new signal deliberately, and says why: a list read has nowhere
honest to put it, and the nightly pass is where the same truncation is already counted.

**The `in-build` sweep.** `in-build` is the register's most misleading status — it tells a reader
work is actively underway — and `lint:ledger-staleness` structurally cannot catch a wrong one: it
compares a node against its slice's status fragment, and a documentation-only branch produces a
perfectly plausible fragment. So every node at `in-build` was checked against the repository
instead. Six were wrong, in both directions:

- **`documents.file-manager.file-inspector` → `not-started`.** It was `in-build` on a remote branch
  carrying a single documentation commit and no code; there is no inspector route, no inspector
  module, and no design under `docs/specs/`. Not `designed` either — the design is unmerged, so
  there is no accepted spec for that status to point at.
- **`documents.ocr.raster-cap` → `shipped`**, and **`platform.schema-migration.monotonic-ids` →
  `shipped`.** Both pointed at a branch (in the second case at an active-work note that no longer
  exists) while the capability had reached `main` independently, with tests.
- **The docs-maintenance system → `shipped` for per-merge assembly and the run-report registry,
  `partial` for the parent.** All three named artifacts are on `main`, the deterministic assembler
  runs on every push, and the report registry has entries beyond its baseline; the evidence still
  said "unmerged".

**Five nodes were left alone and the reasoning written down** rather than guessed at, because
`partial` and `in-build` mean different things and choosing between them on a hunch is worse than
naming the ambiguity.
- **A record is now edited in the window that reads it, and the window stops growing before its tabs
do.** Three owner rulings landed in the record window at once.

Editing happens in place. `onEdit` is gone from the shell, so there is no callback a consumer could
hang a second surface off; the header's Edit control raises the shell's own `editing` state, and the
record snippet is handed the mode so one snippet renders values or fields. The tabs are deliberately
not told the mode, which is what makes "the context pane stays read-only in both modes" true by
construction rather than by five record types each remembering it. Edit refuses entry twice over: a
consumer's own reason, and the absence of a commit path, because a mode with no way to save is worse
than no mode. Commit and abandon are the shell's, always the last two controls in that order — a
person aims at the commit without reading it, and a bar whose terminal control is worded differently
per record type costs exactly that.

A record that fits does not scroll. The panel sizes to its content, so a short record opens as a
short window with no scrollbar and no empty band under the last field; only a record that genuinely
cannot fit caps at the viewport, and then the body alone moves. The header and the action bar never
scroll away. The two statements read as contradictory and had been re-litigated more than once, so
they are written into the recipe as one ordered preference with the order stated.

Growth goes to the tabs, not to the record. The left pane stops at a measure wide enough for a
three-column field row and narrow enough that a description is not set across a monitor; everything
past it goes to attachments and history, which are the half that reads better wide. It is a bound
rather than a ratio, which is why the two panes are flex items: a track ratio cannot say "this one
stops and that one carries on".

**And the width token governed nothing until it was measured.** The recipe declared
`max-inline-size: var(--mc-size-record-window)` on a panel that arrives wearing the dialog's own
`max-w-lg`, and a Tailwind utility outranks the components layer whatever the selector — so the
window opened at 512px while its recipe named 1024. The cap is now a utility fed by the same token
(`--container-record-window`, registered in `mergeClasses` so two `max-w-*` classes cannot both
survive the merge), and the recipe says why it is not declared there. The trap is general: any
recipe setting a width on an element that also carries a width utility loses silently, and nothing
scans for it.
- **The file manager's search results were a second, poorer list. They are the matter's own table now,
and the query re-runs when you come back to it.**

Results were rendered as bare rows carrying a name, a folder and a Show button. Everything the matter
table does — sorting, filtering, the column set, right-click, selection, the footer — was absent, so
acting on a result meant navigating away from the result set. That is also why "download all matches"
had been asked for: with no way to select a result, a bulk button was the only exit.

Results now render through `cellFor`, the same renderer the browse table uses, so a result is a row
in every sense. Selecting several and using the existing download action replaces the bulk button
entirely.

**Three defects went with it.**

The dropdown rendered only on `input`. Re-opening the field with a query already in it showed nothing
until a character was added or removed — the query looked lost when it was merely unrendered. Focus
and click now run the same render.

"Open Full Results" sat below the hit list, so it moved every time the list changed length. It rides
the scope line at the top, and is disabled rather than absent while the query is empty.

The panel stayed hidden until a character arrived, which put the scope selector — the one control a
person sets _before_ typing — out of reach. Opening the field opens the panel.

The search field also appears in the results header, where the query is stated, so refining a search
does not mean returning to the masthead. Re-rendering replaces that input, so focus and caret are
restored on each keystroke; without it, typing reverses itself.

Harness: 51 → 56 checks.
- **A conference room is offered under the office it is in, and named by it where the firm has more than one.** The owner's shape: "A location may be Office 1, Room 1; Office 2, Room 2. Where offices are distinct addresses, but rooms are not."

The location picker listed every room under one "Rooms" heading, so a firm with three offices saw three "Conference Room 1"s and no way to tell them apart. It now draws a group per office, in the order the offices come, with rooms belonging to none under a final heading; an office with no bookable rooms is left out rather than drawn as an empty heading. What the field WRITES is the room's own name while the firm has one office, and "Main Office — Conference Room 1" once there is more than one.

Both spellings match back. A location recorded before this, or typed from memory, is a bare name and still finds its room and books it. A bare name that two offices both answer to matches **neither**: booking one of two rooms a person did not choose between is worse than booking none.

The grouping and the written name live in `room-location.ts` beside the matcher, because the module that writes a location is the one that reads it back to book the room — two answers to "what is this room called" would drift within a round.

`firm_resource` still has a firm-wide unique index on `name`, so two offices genuinely cannot hold rooms of the same name yet. That index, meeting links as bookable places with a concurrency ceiling, participants by tag, recurrence and a separate end zone are all specified in `docs/specs/2026-09-15-calendar-places-people-and-recurrence-design.md` and unbuilt.
- A screen starts reading before you click it, and an empty list stops explaining itself.

Every screen used to fetch after it had mounted, which put a whole round trip after the click: chunk, parse, mount, and only then ask the server anything. `app.html` has set `data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover"` since it was written, meaning to spend the 200–400 ms between the pointer settling on a link and the click landing — but that preload runs a route's load function, and 93 of 98 screens had no load that read anything, so it bought the JavaScript and nothing else. Reads move into the load, where they start on hover and resolve out of a shared cache by the time the component mounts.

The same cache ends the re-reads. `/api/v1/me` was being read on every navigation by the (app) guard and again on mount by 38 surfaces, and it is not a cheap call — a control-plane read, a firm Durable Object wake, a permissions join, the channel and flags, the firm name and the membership state. It is now read once and shared, as are the firm's practice areas, its Locations and its roster.

What the screens read through is `@magna-carta/api-client`, the generated client ADR-0066 chose and CI has been regenerating and diff-gating all along while the app hand-wrote 12,389 lines mirroring the same contract beside it. `/matters` is migrated; the rest follow behind a ratchet that can only fall.

Empty lists now say **No Results** — two words, whether the record holds nothing or a filter excludes everything. They used to open with a definition of the domain term ("A packet is the physical thing the firm holds and moves: an envelope, a deed box, a sealed wallet…"), which is the explanatory prose the no-info-lines ruling already forbids everywhere else and whose home is the user guides. Where a filter is what emptied the table, the way back is still there — as the Clear All Filters control, not as a sentence about it. The table no longer accepts an empty state from the surface above it, so there is nothing to get wrong rather than a rule to remember.
- **Every loading state in the app runs through one region, and the placeholder is the component itself.** `LoadingRegion` (`@magna-carta/design-system/loading-region`) renders a surface's real markup over a fixture snippet while its data has not arrived, and one recipe turns the text, media and controls into bones while the frame, the headings, the labels and the column heads stay real. The region takes `loading` and a `label` sentence, is `inert` and `aria-busy` while loading, and owns the rest by having no prop for it. Eighty-nine hand-placed `Skeleton` boxes across thirty-seven files, three loading sentences and two static spinner glyphs are gone; the `./skeleton` export is gone with them, and the box stays only inside the six design-system components that render placeholder rows of their own shape, under one count prop name, `placeholderCount`.

The research behind it ([`docs/research/2026-09-05-skeleton-loading-framework.md`](docs/research/2026-09-05-skeleton-loading-framework.md)) surveyed the libraries that derive a skeleton from the finished component and found that every one of them, runtime or build-time, needs representative content before it can measure anything, and that once a fixture exists the measurement is the part worth dropping. The design is [`docs/specs/2026-09-05-loading-region-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-09-05-loading-region-design.md).

It cannot stray: `lint:one-ui` carries a `hand-placed-loading` rule that fails the Skeleton import or tag, the recipe class, `aria-busy`, a pulsing utility or a loader glyph anywhere in the app, and the same signals inside the design system outside the homes the registry declares; the rule is proved against known-bad input, the region's story asserts the announcement and the inert fixture, and `/developer-console/loading-states` shows every shape beside its settled state.
- **The scoped gate now names the one type error that is not a type error, and three documents that had
gone stale say what is true.**

**A stale workspace link stops looking like broken code.** After merging a trunk that added a package
or an export path, `tsc -b` reports `Cannot find module '@magna-carta/<something>'` against source
that is perfectly correct — workspace links resolve at install time, so the module is genuinely absent
from `node_modules` while the code and the reference graph are both right. It reads exactly like a
real break, and every time it has cost an afternoon of debugging something that was never wrong. The
remedy is `pnpm install`.

`pnpm check:scoped` now says so itself. The type-check step's output is captured rather than inherited,
and on a failure the gate applies the discriminator that was already in the repository and already
scriptable: if the errors carry `TS2307` against a `@magna-carta/` specifier **and**
`tooling/tsconfig-refs --check` reports every generated build config in sync, nothing about the
projects is stale, so the missing module is a stale link — and the gate prints the remedy. Both halves
have to hold. A hint that also fired on ordinary type errors would be worse than no hint, because it
would train everyone to scroll past the one time it is right, so it was verified in three directions:
it fires with a package's workspace links removed, it stays silent on an ordinary `TS2322`, and the
reference check exits non-zero (suppressing the hint) when a `package.json` really has outrun its
generated graph.

**Two trust documents caught up with the bank-charge carve-out.** `packages/trust-jurisdictions/CLAUDE.md`
and the comment on `cited.firmFundsForBankCharges` in `src/data/nevada.ts` both still said the carve-out
was encoded as a citation and not wired, and that the composition guard refused every posting to a
firm-funds node. `composeTrustFirmFundsEntry` and `openTrustFirmFundsNode` shipped on 2026-08-12. Both
documents now describe the carve-out as the **second door** it is — and the invariant they were making
is intact and stated with the same force, because it is still true: `composeTrustEntry`, the door client
money goes through, refuses a firm-funds line **absolutely**, and the second door admits strictly fewer
shapes rather than more. The Nevada comment's four unsettled points are kept and re-cast as what each
was answered with rather than invented: no cap is chosen (the node's zero floor aborts an over-large
charge instead), the carve-out is refused outright on a pooled interest-bearing account the rules exempt
from service charges, the no-commingling guard is unchanged, and the three-way proof carries the cushion
as its own leg.

**The white paper's _Payments_ card capture matches the accepted decision.** It described capture via
"hosted fields / tokenization (e.g. Helcim.js)" — the in-DOM tokenizer that ADR-0181 rejected **by
name** as SAQ A-EP. It now states the hosted payment modal returning an opaque `cardToken`, the
rejection of the in-DOM tokenizer and of the raw-card API, no PAN and no CVV stored, and a payment
surface free of third-party scripts. The payments design spec's note recording that drift is updated
to record it as resolved.

**A trap gets a warning where the mistake is made.** `idempotencyMiddleware` reads the request body
through `context.req.json()` to fingerprint it, which consumes the raw stream. Mounted in front of a
webhook route it destroys the bytes a signature is computed over, and the failure presents as a wrong
shared secret rather than as a consumed body — so the debugging goes into the credential store and
stays there. The middleware now carries that warning on itself, alongside what a signature-verifying
route does instead.
- **Twelve feature-ledger nodes carried a status that asserts no code, over code.** The vocabulary
defines `deferred` as explicitly parked by a decision and `designed` as an accepted design spec with
no code; a capability with three modules, two tables and seven routes is neither. These are factual
claims the tree refutes, and they move on the same ground the evidence sentences moved on in the
previous pass. The register's headline shifts with them: Done 260 to 264, Part-built 103 to 111,
Ahead 218 to 209, Parked 43 to 40, over an unchanged 624 units of work.

| Node                                  | Was           | Now       |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------- |
| `custodian.stocktake`                 | `deferred`    | `partial` |
| `custodian.retention-destruction`     | `designed`    | `partial` |
| `custodian.will-reminders`            | `deferred`    | `partial` |
| `documents.conversion.office`         | `planned`     | `shipped` |
| `documents.conversion.searchable-pdf` | `not-started` | `shipped` |
| `documents.pdf.manipulation`          | `not-started` | `shipped` |
| `locations.usage.custodian`           | `designed`    | `shipped` |
| `locations.usage.documents-billing`   | `not-started` | `partial` |
| `notifications.digest`                | `deferred`    | `partial` |
| `platform.time-model.zone-context`    | `not-started` | `partial` |
| `product-updates.artifact`            | `not-started` | `partial` |
| `user-docs.admin-docs`                | `not-started` | `partial` |

**Three were found in this pass rather than the last one, all by the same search.**
`documents.pdf.manipulation` read "No merge/split/rotate/flatten module in `crates/pdf-core/src`" —
all four are built, three in `generate.rs` and form flattening in `forms.rs`, and every one is
exposed at the WASM edge. It read `not-started` because it looked for a module of its own; there is
not one, and `documents.pdf.generate` already claimed the same file.
`documents.conversion.searchable-pdf` read "no text-layer writer in `crates/pdf-core`" —
`searchable.rs` is exactly that, wired through `containers/ocr`'s `/ocr/searchable` and a registry
edge. `platform.time-model.zone-context` read "no zone column in `packages/locations/src`", a fact
two other areas had already been corrected on.

**Shipped versus partial was decided by scope coverage, not by deployment.** The two container
engines are `shipped` because `documents.conversion.raster` is, on identical evidence and an equally
undeployed image; inventing a distinction between them would be a new inconsistency rather than a
corrected one. Every leaf that gained a built status gained a `surface:`, all `awaiting-screen`
except `product-updates.artifact`, which is a build step and a KV publish and has no user surface by
nature.

**Six parked nodes said why they were parked without saying which decision parked them**, which
`deferred` and `cut` are required to carry. All six turned out to be parked in a document that names
them — ADR-0054, ADR-0059, or a white-paper topic — so each now cites it.
- **The calendar screen: one View menu, the date as its heading, and three firm calendars.** `calendar-toolbar.svelte` leads with the arrows and the window's name as a heading that opens `MonthJump` (new in `@magna-carta/design-system/calendar`, beside a `compact` density of `Calendar` that the rail's month now uses), and ends with Today and one View menu carrying the views, the week and day's concurrency choice and the agenda's Hide settled. The Kinds filter and `schedule-narrowing.ts` are removed. `calendar-sources.ts` splits the firm's records into `caseSettings` and `deadlines` sources, each with its own read in `calendar-reads.ts`; every rail name is Title Case. `CalendarGrid.Month` keeps its caption for assistive technology only when it has nothing to say, so a month that fills its host no longer overflows it by the caption's line. `formatMonthName` joins the civil-date formatters. Deadline sources read "Court Order" and "Firm".
- **Every sequence the platform draws is now shaped by a scheme, and the numbering screen is eight folds instead of one long menu.** The register's `fixed` formulation is retired (`packages/sequence-numbering/src/purposes.ts`): `invoice`, `time_entry` and `communication` join the five already scheme-shaped, so `SchemeNumberingPurpose` is `NumberingPurpose` and a new run is a row rather than a renderer. Three additions made that reach without changing an issued number. `month`, `day` and `matter_number` join `NumberSegment`, its zod union and `renderNumber`, so the day-scoped call number and the matter-prefixed entry number are templates rather than special cases. `scopeSource: "segments" | "owner"` on the register says whether the counter scope is derived from the template's scoping parts (the collision-proof general case) or passed by the domain — a time entry counts within its matter's handle, an invoice within the letterhead chosen at finalize — and `schemeSchemaFor` refuses a scoping mark on an owner-scoped run, since the switch would do nothing. `scopeDistinguishedBy` names the part such a scheme must carry (time entries: `matter_number`); the invoice run's is conditional and `finalizeInvoice` refuses `unknown-number-scope` by name for a bill drawn under a scope its scheme cannot render. Its mirror, `invoice-numbering-needs-letterhead`, refuses a firm-wide bill once the scheme prints the office code, where the bill would otherwise have reached the renderer and failed as a server error. `renderInvoiceNumber`, `renderEntryNumber`, `renderCommunicationNumber` and their start-value constants are gone; `planSchemeDraw` gained `{ scopeKey, count }` and returns a `SchemeDrawPlan` carrying every number of a block, over the new `guardedAdvanceStatement(…, by)`. The call counter's scope keys are re-keyed by `20261002T192145_communication-number-scope-parts.sql` from `2026-09-08` to the `2026:09:08` the scoping parts derive. On the web surface, `settings/numbering/+page.svelte` is an `Accordion.Root type="multiple"` with the current example on each heading; `numbering-scheme-editor.svelte` puts reorder and delete at the row's end, sizes cells to content, states `preview.parts[index]` in a cell the purpose cannot customize, and offers the starters as "Load an example" in the table's last row. `tooling/lint-settings-scroll/` walks all 27 settings routes through their component graph and fails a nested scroll region, with 15 stated allowances. Two defects the static scan cannot see were found by rendering the page: the parts table was still 1038px in an 848px column because each `ChoicePicker` asked for a text input's default width, which a content-sized table takes as a column floor (the picker gains `fillsCell`, Part alone takes the spare width, the long heading wraps, the row controls are `icon-sm`; `apps/web/test/numbering-parts-table.test.ts` pins it), and `NavigationLayout`'s content-box navigation column was `h-full`, so its gutters overshot the row by 48px and scrolled the canvas on every settings page (it is `self-stretch` now, and the layout's Storybook story measures that neither column passes the layout's bottom).
- **Firm Profile is the firm's name alone; the marks moved to a new Firm Brand page, and Rooms and Resources moved under Firm.** `settings/firm-profile/+page.svelte` drops its offices plate (a copy of the Offices register) and its brand-images plate; the plate moved unchanged to `settings/firm-brand/`, registered as the `firm-brand` section in `apps/web/src/lib/settings/settings-sections.ts` and gated on the same `firm:manageProfile` the brand-image routes enforce. The `resources` section's group is now `firm`, and its catalog's actions column is one `DropdownMenu` behind an icon-sized trigger rather than a button per act.
- **Background blur's Rust path has its first number.** The owner chose to build blur memory-safely, Rust first, on 2026-11-09, and asked for image backgrounds on the same mask. The first slice-2 measurement is recorded as an amendment to `docs/research/2026-09-20-browser-media-effects.md`. `tract-tflite` cannot load MediaPipe's SelfieSegmenter as it stands, because of one custom operator, `Convolution2DTransposeBias`. With a small safe-Rust handler for that operator, the model runs in `wasm32` with SIMD at a p95 of 13.3 ms per inference and matches the reference interpreter exactly. The module is 2.17 MB gzipped, over the 1.5 MB budget. The `meetings.backgrounds-and-noise` ledger node records both rulings and drops its `awaiting-owner` question.
- **A directory person is one scrolling page, entered and read alike.** `record-sections.svelte` stacks every section of a record on one page with a jump rail that lights the section in view (`record-sections.ts` holds the scroll arithmetic and the Show All cap), and both the New Person dialog and the entity window compose it in place of vertical tabs. Pronouns and Dates fold into one About section; `personDraftSummary` reads the draft back as values rather than counts; the entity window's facts move into `entityWindowSubtitle` and its context pane is passed only when a host hands over standing, so `entityWindowFacts` is gone; the matters and relationship panes cap at five rows with Show All; New Person's commit says Save.
- **Screens stop re-reading the session, and arriving at a matter read a moment ago is instant.** `readSession` (`apps/web/src/lib/matters/matters-api.ts`), which about forty-five surfaces call on mount, now answers from the one query cache under the same key the (app) guard fills on the way in (`meGetQueryKey`), at the session-stable ceiling. Each of those screens used to pay a full `/api/v1/me` round trip, in series, before its own read could start. `readSession(fetch, { fresh: true })` and `sessionPermissions.reread` skip the cache for the one write that changes the session under a screen (the Beta Branch switch). A refusal is never cached. The (app) guard drops the cached session before sending somebody to the joining screen, so their return with a firm is judged on a fresh answer rather than bounced back on the cached "no firm yet".

The `/matters/[id]` layout reads the matter through the cache at the record staleness (`readMatterRecord`, `apps/web/src/lib/matters/matter-record.ts`) when arriving, and from the server when the matter already on screen is re-read (`invalidateAll` after a status change or a renumbering). Recording where the paper file is kept drops the cached record. Home starts the Today card's reads from its route load, so the hover preload begins them before the click.
- **The model catalog is the current Anthropic generation, the AI settings screen checks it against Anthropic's own model list, and the screen scrolls once.** `packages/inference/src/catalog.ts` is catalog version 4 (effective 2026-11-09): the reasoning roster is `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` alone, and by the owner's ruling no previous-generation model is offered (`claude-opus-4-8` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` leave; a firm that pinned one reads as following the platform, because the setting read is total); by the owner's decision the `most-capable` tier (the platform default) moves to `claude-opus-5-5` and `balanced` to `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the utility slot moves from `claude-haiku-4-5` (earliest published retirement 2026-10-15, past) to `claude-haiku-5-5`, which nothing called; every entry gains a `displayName`, and every provider model records the effort levels it accepts (`effortLevels`, all five of low, medium, high, xhigh and max) and its own `defaultEffort` (medium for Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, high for Sonnet 5.5), which the entry schema checks; and every lifecycle and confidentiality fact was re-read on 2026-11-09 from Anthropic's model-deprecations and zero-data-retention pages. The Fable line stays out: it requires 30-day retention and is refused under zero data retention. New `packages/inference/src/provider-roster.ts` reads `GET /v1/models` through the injected `HttpClient` and reconciles it with the catalog (per entry, published or not; uncurated models listed as awaiting verification, never selectable); `apps/api-worker/src/inference/provider-roster-source.ts` composes it with an optional `ANTHROPIC_MODELS_API_KEY` secret, a three-second timeout and the Workers Cache API (six hours on success, five minutes on failure), and logs a failed read through `logOperationFailed`. `GET /api/v1/firm/ai/settings` gains `models[].displayName`, `models[].published`, `models[].effortLevels`, `models[].defaultEffort` and a `provider` object. On the web surface, the model picker names models by their display name, the facts list gains Model, Effort Levels and Provider's Live List rows, the section's label and title are now "AI", and `SettingsScrollRegion` is now `relative`, so LoadingRegion's absolutely positioned announcer no longer stretches the shell's `<main>` into a second scrollbar (`apps/web/test/settings-scroll-region-containment.test.ts`).
- **A conflicts check names who ran it and who it searched.** The report's opening statement names the acting member from the roster (`readMemberDisplayName`) instead of quoting their handle, and reads "as a preliminary check" rather than "trigger preliminary". Each run summary and each row of the firm's log carries `subjectParties`, named from one set-valued Directory read; the check page lists them under Parties and the log gains a Parties column. A check filed on no matter reads No Matter.
- **The notification centre is the product's one grid.** `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/notifications`
renders on `DataTable.Grid` with a declared column model (`notification-columns.ts`): a leading
read-state check, Notification, Details, Matter, Category, Priority and When, with Dismiss or Restore
pinned to the trailing edge on every row. The Everything/Unread toggle and the category select are
gone; their questions are the Status and Category column filters. The feed reads unread and read
rows together (`state` on `GET /api/v1/notifications` now repeats), and the dismissed rows are a
second read the member opens from the foot of the table, ordered after the live rows and drawn
quiet. New route `POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/restore` returns a dismissed row to the feed as
read. Priority shows only Urgent or Needs Attention; informational rows have no word. The bell tray
leads with the most pressing of its rows, says "No Results" when empty, and links to "Open
Notifications". The `email.filed` kind now reads "Email saved to a matter".
- **Client and matter numbering: separators, unpadded counts, and an editor that drags.** `NumberSegment`'s `date_opened` and `client_name` take an optional `separator` (`-`, `.`, `_`, `~` or empty; a slash is refused because a number is URL-safe), mirrored in the OpenAPI `NumberSegment` schema and the generated client. Absent renders as before (`20261111`, `AshcombeMercantile`), so no saved scheme changes shape; a client name's words are now folded one at a time and joined by the separator, dropping a word that folds to nothing. In `numbering-scheme-editor.svelte`, Preview sits under Current with no descriptive line under either (Current keeps its line only when nothing is in force), parts move by a grip on `DragReorderController` with Alt+Arrow as the keyboard path, the move buttons and the examples (`NUMBERING_STARTERS`) are gone, "Digits" is "Format" (counter minimum digits, year digits, separators), "Restarts the Count" is "Separate Count", the Part picker shows each kind's sample value, and a new counter starts at one digit. `compareGridRows` orders text with a numeric `Intl.Collator`, so every `DataTable.Grid` text column sorts `3333-2` before `3333-10`.
- **A returning reader's browser no longer re-asks for the application's files.** Cloudflare's asset
server answers every file with `max-age=0, must-revalidate` unless told otherwise, so each repeat
visit to the sign-in page made about 116 conditional requests (a `304` each) before the application
could start. `magna-carta-web` now serves everything under `/_app/immutable/`, whose names carry a
hash of their content, with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Measured against
`wrangler dev` with Chromium on 2026-11-10: a first visit is unchanged at 120 requests, and a repeat
visit reaches the server once, for the page itself.

**The same change makes a missing application file a `404`.** `magna-carta-web` gains its first
script (`apps/web-worker/src/`), run only for `/_app/*`. The single-page fallback used to answer a
request for a script that was not there with the application shell and a `200`; with a year-long
lifetime that would have let a deploy race store HTML under a script's address. The script answers
`404` with `no-store` instead, and only a response that really is the file gets the lifetime. The
Worker still binds nothing but its own public files. Home: `docs/conventions/operations.md`, the
`magna-carta-web` roster entry.
- **Capital letters and accents do not matter when searching inside files.** The keyword engine (`crates/search-core`) now composes a letter and its accent into one character before it cuts text into words (text taken out of a PDF often carries the two apart, which used to cut "Peña" into "pen" and "a"), folds Latin letters to their unaccented form, and lowercases, so "pena" finds "Peña" and "resume" finds "résumé" inside a document as they already do in a note. The same is done to a quoted word in a question, so the search box sends a finished word as typed. An unfinished word is a pattern, which the engine compares with the index's words as held, so `packages/search/src/keyword-query.ts` folds that one itself from `keyword-letter-folds.ts`, a table rendered from the one the engine writes out about its own analyzer (`crates/search-core/tests/fixtures/body-letter-folds.tsv`); a test on each side holds the three together. This changes how every word is cut, so it is schema generation 2, taken now because no production index exists yet and afterwards it would mean rebuilding every one. The address index (`crates/address-core`) is packaged in the same split format and used to borrow that generation number; it now carries its own (`ADDRESS_INDEX_GENERATION`, the value its partitions already hold), so the partitions in the bucket stay readable. Internal for now on the same ground as the entries before it: nothing inside a file is searchable in production until the search worker is deployed and bound.
- **The api-worker tests that never reach the Workers runtime now run in plain Node, and test and type-check memory have explicit ceilings.** A test file that declares `// @node-runtime` in its header runs in a second project, `apps/api-worker/vitest.node.config.ts`, with no workerd VM and no whole-app preload. That preload cost about 25 s of setup per file and most of the suite's 6.4 GB peak. The first 67 files to opt in run together in about 8 s. The other test projects share a ceiling of eight workers (`MC_TEST_MAX_WORKERS`) instead of one per CPU, and `tsc -b` runs with a 4 GB heap instead of Node's default, which is sized from system memory. On a 15 GB machine that default is 2,096 MB, against a measured peak of 1,943 MB. Measurements and reasoning: `docs/conventions/build-performance.md`, under "Test memory".
- **A change made in Outlook is picked up when it happens.** Each connected account now asks Microsoft
to say when anything in the member's calendar changes, and a notice brings that account's sync pass
forward to about a second away, where it used to wait for the next pass and could take six hours.
The notice is believed only by a secret the account gave Microsoft, carries nothing that is read
about the change, and is received on a new public address, `POST
/api/v1/calendar-sync/provider-notices/microsoft/{firmId}/{connectionId}`. The six-hour pass stays
as the backstop for a lost notice. A request for a pass that arrives while one is running is now
run straight after it. Dormant until a Microsoft application is registered.
- **An edit made in Outlook changes the event in Magna Carta.** A member who may edit the calendar
and moves, renames or re-places their Outlook copy of an event now changes the event itself, for
everyone it is shared with, where before the copy became a question on their Calendar Sync page.
The change goes through the calendar's own edit, is recorded under the member's name, and is marked
in the audit log as having come from their calendar. A member without permission to edit the
calendar is still asked. A deleted copy never cancels an event, a deadline's copy is still put
back, a title is not carried from a copy sent with minimal detail, and a series cannot be moved to
a different first day from Outlook. Dormant until a Microsoft application is registered.
- **Caller lookup names the town and the time there.** The free answer of `communications.callerLookup` now carries, beside the area code's region, `place` (the town the number's exchange was assigned to, from libphonenumber's exchange-level geocoding rows) and `timeZone` (the IANA zone of the number's prefix, from libphonenumber's time zone map; null where the prefix spans several). Both tables are generated by `packages/caller-lookup/scripts/refresh-places.mjs`. The record screen shows "702 · Henderson, Nevada" and "3:19 PM PST".
- **The Changelog lists every merged pull request.** `/updates` now reads `docs/pull-request-ledger.json`, which `tooling/doc-fragments/build-pull-request-ledger.mjs` rebuilds from first-parent history: one row per squash-merged pull request with its number, commit, landing day, the application areas its paths fall in (four or more read as "Across the app", none as "Behind the scenes"), and the developer text of the fragment it added. The assemble-docs workflow rebuilds it whenever a merge carries a fragment, and the docs-sync routine runs it as a backstop. The screen (`pull-request-changelog.svelte`) groups rows by day and folds each day and each pull request on a leading caret (`Accordion.Trigger` gains `chevron="start"`), puts each pull request on a card with linked pull-request and commit badges, and filters by kind, area and whether members see the change from three compact menus.
- **Community board, Topic.** The composer asks for a post's topic from a dropdown instead of a wall
of product-area buttons, and the board's rail and a post's details call it Topic as well.
- **The Certificate of Completion reads as a finished document.** The sheet opens with the product's lockup and a title in the application's dark gold, with rules in the same colour; the summary, the signers and the audit log each start a page of their own. The reference is now a number a person can read out, `MC-` and the first twelve characters of the document hash in three groups (`certificateReference` in `packages/signing/src/certificate.ts`, carried on the record as `reference`), where it was the request's internal identifier; that identifier stays in the record and the plain text as `Record` and is no longer printed on the sheet, and neither is a signer's internal identifier. The first page carries everything a reader wants at a glance: the sender as `Sender: Name` and `Sender: Email`; every instant as a date row and a time row; the count of signers, signatures and initials; a table of the signers with when each signed and how many signature and initial blocks each completed (`SigningIntent.signatureCount` and `initialCount`, which the seal route accepts; a signer whose blocks were not counted is one signature and no initials); and a Contact note in small text naming who answers for the document (`SigningEnvelope.contact`, or the sender without one) and who answers for the certificate (the platform, with the address in the sign Worker's `CERTIFICATE_SUPPORT_EMAIL` variable when it is set). Each signer's full record is on the next page and the audit log on the one after. Labels are in title case and the footer reads `Certificate MC-...` beside the page number. Two lines are gone: the note that times are as the server observed them, and the paragraph explaining the document hash. The first page holds the summary, eight signers and the contacts, so a certificate for eight people prints its front on one sheet: rows are set closer together and the top and bottom margins are three quarters of an inch. To draw this, the PDF composer (`crates/pdf-compose-core`) learned three things, each off unless a document asks: an `accent` colour, which its title, first two heading levels and rules are drawn in; `compact`, which narrows the rows of every table and field list; and a `small` paragraph, set in the caption's size. A document that names none of them is written exactly as before. The lockup is a picture (`packages/signing/src/brand-lockup.ts`) rendered once from the design system's `BrandMark`, because a page cannot load the blackletter web font.
- **A conflicts check's run list is now its History tab, and Assign to Matter sits beside Print.** The check's second tab reads History and drops its introductory line. A check with no matter is assigned to one from an **Assign to Matter** button in the header, next to Print Report and Download Report, which opens the matter field in a small panel; the field no longer sits at the foot of the Details section.
- **A conflicts check reads names in calls, texts, tasks and Magnus through the record index.** `packages/conflicts/src/content-search.ts` asks `@magna-carta/search`'s record index for each subject party's names as exact phrases, firm-wide and index-led, instead of scanning those tables with LIKE. Matching is by whole word and folds case and accents. Each name keeps at most `NAME_RESULT_CEILING` (200) records per place, and the check's `inputs.places` records `namesAtCeiling`, which the report states. Numbers, addresses, linked records and email (not an index source) are matched on their own columns as before.
- **The conflicts check is redesigned, and a run can be cancelled.** The New Check panel asks for parties only and lists five locations, each a dropdown of what it searches; Firm Employees runs without a matter by looking for members among the entities a check reached (`findMemberEntities`). The check page gains Report and Runs tabs, collapsible Details, Status and Results sections, a per-location status log, result cards with filters and a review dropdown, and icon-only print and download buttons. `POST /api/v1/conflicts/checks/{checkId}/runs/{runId}/cancel` stops a run; a run summary reports `cancelled`, `cancelledByUserId` and `askedScope`. Reports say "0 results." and count results rather than candidates.
- **New Person's form is wider beside the duplicate check.** A primary pane that carries a section rail now stops at the new `size.record-form` token (832px: the record's 640px measure plus the rail) instead of `size.record-pane`, through `.mc-modal-frame-pane:has([data-record-rail])` in `modal-frame.css`. `record-sections.svelte` marks its rail. A three-field name row and the email row's kind, address and use now fit on one line.
- **HEVC and MKV recordings play where the browser can decode them.** The server no longer refuses
HEVC video, or Matroska files whose tracks carry browser codecs (H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9 or AV1 with
AAC, Opus, Vorbis or FLAC sound); the player offers the download when the reader's own browser
reports a media error or shows no picture. ProRes, MPEG-2 and Dolby Digital sound stay download-only.
A per-firm data migration clears every stored `download-only` verdict once, so videos refused under
the old rule are judged again the next time they are opened.
- **The Magnus transcript is laid out as an exchange.** The design-system Conversation component gains
a second arrangement (`arrangement="exchange"` on `Conversation.Transcript`, with new `TurnMark`,
`TurnContent` and `TurnActions` parts); the default `record` arrangement and the meetings chat are
unchanged. `magnus-transcript.svelte` uses it: member turns on the right under the conversation
creator's real name and initials (the session read for the signed-in member, the firm roster for
anyone else), Magnus on the left behind the blackletter M, a time on every turn and a Copy control.
The conversation head names the matter it is kept on beneath the title, with its number, read
through `matter-citations.svelte.ts`. First piece of the owner's round two in
`docs/conventions/magnus-rulings.md`.
- **Meetings say plainly when the video service is not connected.** The Meetings page and a meeting's room no longer tell a member that meetings were not turned on for their firm and that an administrator should fix it; they say the video service that carries meetings is not connected to the site yet.
- **Meeting recording ships switched off until the deployment is set up for it.** Recording,
transcripts, summaries and live captions are now on `main`, but the recording queue
(`MEETING_RECORDING_COMPOSE`) is left unbound in `apps/api-worker/wrangler.jsonc`, because a deploy
that binds a queue the account does not have fails. The start route now also requires that queue
before it offers recording. The owner's steps are in the operations runbook under "Turning meeting
recording on".
- **One field for a day and a time.** The design system's new `DateTimeField`
(`@magna-carta/design-system/date-time-field`) holds a day, a time of day, or both: the parts are
typed into one box, and its button opens one panel with the month beside a list of times, or only
the half the field asks for. The list steps every fifteen minutes but the field takes any minute, and
an off-step time is listed in its place (`time-choices.ts`). `formatWallClockTime` joins the display
vocabulary for a time with no day or zone. The calendar's event form uses it for Starts and Ends,
replacing a date picker beside the browser's time box and the All Day checkbox, which is now the
Starts list's first row. `withStartsOn` and `withStartsAtTime` (`event-draft.ts`) carry the start
date to the end and put a new end an hour after the start.
- **The PDF engine's forms code is split by what it does, and the crate has an area note.** `crates/pdf-core/src/forms.rs` was 3,255 lines holding the field-tree walk, the text-field drawing, the fill and flatten writers and 1,750 lines of tests. It is now `src/forms/`: `mod.rs` (types, the walk, `read_form`), `appearance.rs`, `fill.rs`, `flatten.rs` and `tests.rs`. Code was moved, not changed: the public functions and types, the WebAssembly exports and all 319 unit tests are the same. `crates/pdf-core/CLAUDE.md` is new and says where each operation lives and the rules every new one must follow.
- **The person form is tidier, and a ZIP code fills in the town.** `HonorificField` rows carry the whole line they leave as their `label`, because the combobox writes the chosen row's label into the input: picking "Jr." then "Esq." had shown "Esq." alone while the record held "Jr., Esq.". `LabelledField` now renders an error `sr-only` and as the control's `title`, and `input.css` / `combobox.css` paint `aria-invalid` controls with `status-danger`, so no field grows a line of text under it. `AddressFields` puts the country last and marks a malformed postal code as invalid rather than hinting. New Person's other names are full name blocks opened by Add Other Name (`filledOtherNames` drops empty ones); the address, identifier and organization entry rows start as Add buttons; the contact and address "Use" is labelled "Type"; and the address place/mailing choice is no longer asked (a new address is recorded as physical). `@magna-carta/address-formats/us-postal-places` adds `usPostalPlaceFor`, generated from the GeoNames postal-code file (CC BY 4.0) and loaded lazily.
- **The player's new look, a settings menu, screenshots and sound files.** The video player lays its
controls over the picture on the chrome ink and fades them while the video plays; resting on the
seek bar shows the time and the frame there. Speed (now a submenu), Copy Link at, Save Screenshot
and Download moved into a settings menu behind a cog, and picture in picture is gone. A screenshot
saves the frame on screen as a PNG named for the video and the moment. For that, the cookieless
files host grants CORS read access to the app's own pages (never a wildcard). MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV,
FLAC and Ogg sound files are now judged and play in the same player, drawn as a panel of controls.
- **The Record Communication window is built around the phone number, and holds several calls at once.** `communication-fields.svelte` now leads with Call / Text and Incoming / Outgoing as a pressed button group (`$lib/components/button-choice.svelte`), then `PhoneNumberField`, then the notes, then a one-line When that opens on Change; the Contact field leaves the form while a record is being made. The window (`communication-record-window.svelte`) holds a list of `CallEntry` drafts down the left of the pane, each the draft on screen rather than a copy; saving one retires it and the window closes on the last, and `recordThenIntake` no longer closes the window, so the messaging page stopped closing it too. While creating, the context tabs are Identification (`communication-identification.svelte`: the contact, their open matters read through `readDirectoryEntityMatterParties` with a search past five, and File Here) and History (`communication-number-history.svelte`: the log's own search, narrowed to rows on the same stored number). Start An Intake moved into the header menu; the subtitle is the previewed number alone, in italics. The contact choice moved to `communication-contact.ts` so the form and the panel share it.
- **The text a firm holds in its records is now indexed, and matter search reads that index for prose.** A per-firm migration adds the record index: `record_text_entry` and the contentless full-text table `record_text_fts`, kept current only by triggers on `matter_note`, `time_entry`, `cost_entry`, `matter_event`, `communication`, `matter_task`, `magnus_conversation` and `magnus_turn`, and filled in the same migration for records that already exist. The sources are declared once in `packages/search/src/record-index-sources.ts` and everything else is rendered from them. `packages/matter-search` now matches notes, time, costs, calendar and the words of a call or text through the index; files, folders, parties, custody, billing and telephone numbers still match by substring. Tasks and Magnus conversations are indexed and have no reader yet. Design: `docs/specs/2026-11-10-indexing-and-discovery-design.md`.
- **Screenshots and converted copies are filed beside the recording.** Save Screenshot now files the
still into the matter, in the recording's folder, instead of saving it to the reader's computer. The
PNG carries its provenance in UTF-8 text chunks (Title, Description, Source, Comment, Creation Time,
Author), written by `apps/web/src/lib/documents/recording-still.ts`. A recording that will not play
now reads "Unreadable Media File" and, for an MP4, QuickTime or Matroska file whose refusal is about
its encoding, offers Convert to MP4. The playable copy is saved as a file of its own beside the
original ("<name> (converted).mp4"), through the same reserve, write, complete and ingest path as
any server-written document, and the original's version records it in the new
`playable_copy_file_id` column. A copy a member deletes is owed again on the next request.
- **A search result marks the words that answered, and a long text is quoted where they are.** Every hit of a matter's own search (`matterSearch.search`) and of the search across matters (`search.acrossMatters`) gains `titleMarks` and `snippetMarks`: where each run of the reader's words begins and ends in the text beside it, as offsets in UTF-16 code units with the end not included (the new `SearchTextMark` component). The words are found again on the server by the rules of the index that made the match (`packages/search/src/matched-text.ts`): a whole word, the start of the last word typed or a quoted run for the record index and for the file contents index, each by its own cutting and folding, and the characters typed for a name or a number. Each source of the matter search declares which rule its title and its excerpt are marked by, or none (`marking` in `packages/matter-search/src/sources/all.ts`), so a title that is a date is left alone and a file found by the words inside it marks the sentence and not the name. **`snippet` changes for a long record:** a text matched through the record index that runs past about two hundred characters is now cut to the stretch holding the most of the question, with an ellipsis at a cut end, where it used to be the whole column; a shorter text is unchanged. The marking is the last step of both searches, after the matter binding, the visible-matter predicate and the limit, and cannot add, drop or reorder a result. Additive on the wire apart from the shorter `snippet`; no migration and no binding. Not built: marks in the Matters and People groups of the Search page, which are read from the matters listing and the directory.
- **The favourite star moves into the page menu.** `page-actions-menu.svelte` now opens with Add to Favorites (Remove from Favorites, with the star glyph filled gold, once the page is saved), ahead of Copy Link and Open in New Tab, and `ScreenHeader` no longer draws a separate star. `favorite-control.svelte` is removed; the favourites store is unchanged, so every saved favourite carries over. `favoritable={false}` still drops the whole menu. The ruling is updated in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.
- **Task comments stand beside the task.** The comment thread moved out of the task window's tabs into a column of its own on the right, so it stays in view whichever tab is open. `RecordWindow` gains an optional `aside` snippet (with `asideLabel`), a fixed column after the tabs sized by the new `size.record-aside` token; a window carrying one opens to `size.record-window-wide` (the `max-w-record-window-wide` utility), so the panel is added beside the record and its tabs rather than taken from them. Without `aside` the window renders exactly as before.
- **The Tasks list and the task window, rebuilt on the firm's lists, statuses and teams.** `task-list.svelte` is now a `DataTable.Grid` over `TaskRow` (`task-columns.ts`): a status pill per row (`task-status-menu.svelte`) offering the statuses the list's flow allows plus Mark Complete; Start, Due and Priority edited in the row (`task-date-field.svelte`, `editTaskFields`); sub-tasks read with `readSubtaskTrees` and kept under their parent by `orderTaskRows`, folding from a chevron; bands keyed by the root task with Group By defaulting to List; a View menu for one or two lines, row size and columns; Me Mode (`mine=assigned|watching|both`); Show Completed (`completed=false` by default); and a Task Settings dialog (`task-settings-dialog.svelte`) for lists, statuses, flow and teams behind `tasks:managePlans`. A past due date is drawn red and never labelled. `task-record-window.svelte` edits in place (`editControl={false}`), keeps Save for a new task, puts the status beside Mark Complete, moves Duplicate, Archive and Delete into the "..." menu, and adds People, Location with Join, Checklist, Sub-Tasks and Links. The rung buttons and the Overdue badge are gone from both screens, and the print sheet names the status and Completed rather than the rung.
- **The app worker is bound to the keyword search engine.** `apps/api-worker/wrangler.jsonc` declares the `SEARCH_SERVICE` service binding to `magna-carta-search`, on the owner's confirmation of 2026-11-13 that the worker is on the account. No code path changed: `resolveSearchIndexPort` now returns the port over the binding in place of the deferred one, the engine generation changes (`index:none` to `index:search`) so the index queue attempts its parked documents again, and a matter's search, the conflicts check and a discovery review set can ask the engine. `searchServiceConnected` on `GET /api/v1/firm/search-settings` and `fileContents.serviceConnected` on `GET /api/v1/firm/search-status` read true. A firm's files are still indexed only after that firm turns indexing on. The test pool binds a stub for the service that refuses every operation, so a test reads the binding as present by default and passes an environment without it to reach the deferred port. **A conflicts check is given no way to the file index for a firm that has not turned file indexing on** (`apps/api-worker/src/conflicts/file-contents-searcher.ts`, now asynchronous): with the service bound, a searcher there would have had every matter answer that no file names the party, and the check would have recorded `files` as `searched` when no file had been read.
