**Four hand-written sections became one component.** `version-panel-section.svelte` owns the heading,
the fold, the failure block and the loading region; each section still decides its own name, pills,
skeleton, failure sentence and rows. The wording had already started to drift between the four
copies. The folds are a registry too, keyed by section id — the fourth section had arrived without
the doc comment the other three carried and without the file's own header sentence being updated.

**Rows link to the things they name.** A Worker's name links to its Cloudflare dashboard page through
the account-agnostic `?to=/:account/…` form, so the link embeds no account identifier and works for
every member of the account. A commit links to the commit, on the parts a reader actually reads a
diff for — this build, the API, and the Worker serving this page — and the Update Available block
links to the diff between the running bundle and the one being served. Nothing is linked that cannot
be verified: a placeholder commit or an unresolved repository renders as plain text. The repository is
resolved at build time from the git remote (`resolveRepositoryUrl` in the shared commit-identity
script), so a fork links to itself.

**`GET /api/v1/meta/versions` reports what each probe cost.** The number was being paid for and thrown
away. Every probe is raced against a fixed timeout, so "reported" and "unreachable" are two ends of
one measurement with nothing between them — a Worker answering just inside the timeout read as
perfectly healthy until it flipped. Rows carry their latency and a slow one is marked.

**The panel can file what it is showing.** Report an Issue opens the same dialog every other surface
uses, carrying the panel's whole diagnosis; `POST /api/v1/incidents` accepts it as a bounded,
optional `context.deployment`, redacted by construction like every other field there. Previously the
only route was copy, close, find the profile menu, paste — four steps during an incident, each of
which can lose the paste.

**The panel is reachable from search, and so is the next tool of its shape.** The command palette
renders registries and never hand-lists an item, but every registry it had described a
_destination_ with an href. A surface that opens in place had no registry to join, so
`$lib/developer/diagnostic-actions.ts` is the one for that shape — an id, a label, the words it
should be findable by, whether this build offers it, and the function that runs. The panel's open
state moved out of the component (`build-panel.svelte.ts`) so a registry entry can reach it.

**The chip says which build mode it is, outside production.** Two screenshots of one commit, one from
a preview deploy and one from the real site, were indistinguishable.

**And the panel is finally tested in a browser.** Its component rules are asserted by regex over its
source, because the node pool cannot mount a design-system component — the right trade for what those
rules pin, and unable to tell you the panel opens at all. `e2e/build-panel.spec.ts` drives the real
thing: the sections settle, a fold survives a reload, the palette opens it, and a signed-out panel
issues no authenticated request.

**Merged onto the report extraction, not around it.** `main` split the panel into a shared
`version-report.svelte` rendered by both the chip and the new Settings · Versions page while this
branch was open. Everything above is applied to that component, so the page gets all of it too: the
same paste, the same links, the same latency, the same failure blocks. The chip keeps what is the
chip's — the build environment badge, and the popover state the palette opens. One regression from
that extraction is repaired on the way past: the health row had lost its `badgeVariant` passthrough,
so a readiness check reading "Not applicable" was rendering green rather than neutral.
- **The build register renders on `main`, never on a branch.** `docs/now.md`, `docs/now.html` and `docs/decisions-open.html` were rendered by every branch that flipped a `roadmap.d/` node, so any two such branches rewrote the same whole document and conflicted on it: fifteen of the last forty merges to `main` touched the file, and a trust pull request hit the conflict three times in four days on a file nobody had written by hand. The register is a derived view of the trunk, so the trunk renders it, as it already did for `CHANGELOG.md` and the Decision-Log register: the per-merge assembly workflow when it has minutes, the weekly docs-sync routine otherwise. `tooling/doc-fragments/register-renderers.mjs` says who renders (`main`, `docs-assembly`, `docs-sync/*`); `vp run register-build` refuses to write anywhere else (`--preview` shows the render without committing it); and `pnpm run lint:roadmap` holds the files to a fresh render where they are rendered and fails a branch that carries a change to them, with the `git checkout` that restores them. A branch's whole change is its ledger edit.
- **Four corrections on the calendar surface, from the owner's 2026-09-14 round.**

**Whose calendar left the toolbar.** The Mine / Everyone pair and the colleague dropdown beside them are gone: "remove colleague, mine, everyone buttons since that is covered by leftside bar functionality". They were a second mechanism for a question the rail already answers a calendar at a time — a reader wanting their own day turns their own calendar on. The address's `scope=` key is still read, so a link somebody was handed still opens where it says, and `chooseScope` survives for the host whose scope changes under it.

**The event type is a typeahead, sorted.** It was a plain select over a catalog that runs to dozens of hearing, conference and deposition kinds, in whatever order the read handed them over. It is now the same combobox the zone field and the member pickers are, and the list is alphabetical.

**The record form's timing fields are two identical lines and one zone control.** Three defects in one region, all reported: the zone sat in a 40-pixel slot, so its list of continents and cities opened into a field too narrow to read; the Ends line stated the same zone as a _sentence_ where Starts offered a dropdown; and both lines were built from fitted controls, so an empty time field and a filled one were different widths and the two lines drifted out of alignment the moment somebody answered one of them. Starts and Ends are now the design system's `FieldRow` — equal tracks, which cannot do that — and the zone is its own full-width control beneath the two moments it qualifies. `TimeZonePicker` lost its `compact` mode with the slot that needed it; the list still reads by code and name both, because CST is three different zones.

Still open from the same round, and larger than a screen: a separate zone for the end of a setting (one `time_zone` column today), events reaching the calendars of their location and their participants, participants editable in the entry window and addable by tag, one location model over offices, rooms, places in town and meeting links, and recurrence.
- **The calendar's fifth round: the interface taken apart along its own rules.** A modularity review of `apps/web/src/lib/calendar/` found the entry window at 2,150 lines deciding what the module's conventions say a pure module decides, and one host reading what the shared context already held. This round is behaviour-preserving. The window's decisions are pure modules with tests: `entry-verbs.ts` (which verbs a record's state allows, and the tab counts), `entry-updates.ts` (a correction never re-sends participants), `continue-draft.ts` (the fourth draft), `entry-links.ts` (which end of a link is the other one, and what may still be related), `calendar-permission.ts` (the one wording of the calendar-manage refusal, used by the window, the firm screen, the matter section and the three settings catalogs), and `draft-text.ts` (the trim-to-null, wall-clock and civil-date readings the four drafts and three forms each carried a copy of). The Links and Rooms tabs are their own components owning their reads, forms and failures (`entry-links-tab.svelte`, `entry-rooms-tab.svelte`); the window's event, firm-event and continuance panes render `record-timing-fields.svelte` and the new `event-type-select.svelte` instead of six hand-written copies of the same fields, which also ends the drift between "End date" and "End Date". The matter section's List view moves into the module as `matter-calendar-list.svelte`, and the page reads through the shared context, by the owner's ruling. The view's per-scope sentences and addresses move down into `calendar-scope.ts`, `calendar-window.ts` and `calendar-reads.ts`; the untested pure modules gain tests. The window is under 1,300 lines and every question it used to answer inline is asserted without a browser.
- **The matter calendar's Soon line names its real dependency.** It said recording waited on the
participant picker; the picker exists now, and what recording waits on is the event and deadline
forms, which the calendar stream builds. When it does, `participantKind: "entity"` is an
`EntityPicker` pick and an event opened in a record window shows its people on `RecordParties`; a
judge stays an `external` participant by default, as the calendar design rules.
- **The calendar's rail folds, keeps a month in view, and the screen's name spans it.** Three corrections from the owner's 2026-09-16 pass, and one of them widened a shared component.

**A folder folds.** The disclosure is the folder's NAME — chevron and name are one button at the full width of what is left after the checkbox, the shape the application sidebar's own groups take. It is deliberately not the `Accordion` component: that component's trigger IS its whole header, and this header already holds the three-state checkbox, which cannot be nested inside a button. What folds is the LIST, not the head, so the folder's own switch stays reachable whether it is open or shut and folding hides no calendar a reader could otherwise turn on. A shut folder states how many of its calendars are on, because that count is the one fact its hidden rows were carrying. Held per browser beside the colours, and stored as a DEPARTURE like everything else in `calendar-preferences.svelte.ts`, so a folder shipped later arrives open rather than shut because a stored list predates it.

**`NavigationLayout` gained a spanning `header` and a pinned `navigationFooter`.** Both optional; giving neither leaves the DOM byte-identical for Settings, Magnus, Tools and Reports. Neither is calendar-specific — a title naming the SCREEN belongs over the whole canvas rather than over one column of it, and a rail with a picker under it is the shape of every navigation whose last element must stay in view while its list scrolls. The header sits inside the cancelled canvas inset and puts the gutter back itself; `navigationFooter` moves the scroll region and its reserved gutter off the `<nav>` onto an inner stack, because a pinned footer cannot sit inside the thing that scrolls past it. The landmark stays the `<nav>` either way, so what a screen reader announces does not change.

**The masthead spans and the date controls take its old place.** `CalendarView`'s `header` is now a plain `Snippet` that hands nothing back, and the view switch and window navigation sit at the top of the content column in every arrangement. That replaces the 2026-09-14 ruling, which seated them in the masthead's actions beside New — right while the masthead sat over the grid's own column, and wrong the moment it spanned both. One place instead of two, and no host decides.

`calendar-month-picker.svelte` rides the new footer. It moves the ANCHOR and never the view: somebody reading a week who presses a Thursday means that Thursday's week, so it calls `goToDay` rather than `showDay`, and its week begins on the day the firm chose so its columns and the grid's are the same seven days.
- **The firm calendar's rail of calendars moved onto `NavigationLayout`**, the design system's one shape for a screen with a navigational column on the left and content on the right.

It had drawn its own: a `<nav>` at `w-3xs` with a scroll region and a gutter of its own beside the grid — a sixth width and a sixth scroll treatment for the shape the owner ruled on 2026-09-11 is one component. Settings, Magnus, Tools and Reports were already on it; the calendar was the screen nobody had come back to.

`CalendarView` renders the layout where the rail stands — a firm-side scope with calendars to list — and keeps the plain full-height stack everywhere else, so a matter's calendar, a room's grid, Home's card and the record forms' day schedule are untouched. The screen's masthead is handed DOWN as a `header` snippet and drawn at the top of the content column: the layout takes the full height under the top bar and cancels the work canvas inset, so a masthead above the tag would sit above the whole canvas. The Magnus workspace already does this, for the same reason.

The rail's rows stay checkbox rows rather than becoming `NavigationLayout.Row`. The shared row renders its own anchor or button and lights the one the reader is standing on; every row here is a switch with a control already inside it, which cannot be nested in another. What the two columns share is the frame and the indent stagger — the folder heading its group at the column's cap-line, its calendars one step past it — which is precisely what "the layout imposes no structure on what the navigation holds" is for. A calendar's name now wraps rather than truncating, as every other navigation column's does.
- `pnpm check` led with its most expensive and most fragile pass. That is the wrong end: a run that dies
partway reports nothing about the steps behind the one that died, and the type-aware lint pass —
tsgolint over roughly 3,300 files — has been observed OOM-killed at step one of eight in a container,
taking the whole chain down before anything else had spoken.

The two checks that cost seconds and cannot fail spuriously now lead: the build-reference sync, then
the drizzle snapshot freshness that landed a few merges ago specifically to catch a destructive
migration. Both together are under four seconds. Everything slow follows them.

This matters more than the ordering usually would. The gate of record has started no job since
2026-08-05 — an account-side billing block, not a workflow fault — so the whole-repo chain run by hand
is what a merge currently leans on. A chain whose cheap high-signal checks sit behind a pass that can
be killed is one that answers nothing on the machines where it dies.

Also swept nine stream notes for branches that have landed. The registry lists them now rather than
leaving them to be noticed, which is what made a nine-note backlog visible as a single line.
- **The New Check panel has two panes, and every setting says what it searches.** The panel asked for
parties, a matter, a trigger, four source checkboxes, a band, three hop budgets and two caps in one
column, with the meanings on hover and a footer reading `Firm floor · Party · Balanced · Defaults
depth 1 · closure cap 500 · candidate cap 5000`. Almost none of that could be acted on by somebody
who had not built the engine.

It is now two panes. The left one asks the two things a member always fills in — the parties, and
the matter the check is filed under — and under them says, in sentences, what pressing **Run Check**
will actually do: how far it will walk each kind of relationship, whether it can reach the firm's own
people, how names will be compared, and which trigger the log will file it under. The right pane
holds the search settings, each with its own line saying what it searches rather than a hover title.

**The names changed with the layout.** `Party`, `Graph`, `Imputation` and `Content` are now
**Name or identifier**, **Relationship**, **The firm's own people** and **Documents and messages**.
`Strictness` — a dial, not a thing — is **Name matching**, and its two settings, `Balanced` and
`Over-inclusive`, are **Standard** and **Widest**; both say out loud that they match names that
_sound_ alike, which was true before and said nowhere. `Control` and `Family` are **Ownership and
control** and **Family and personal**. `Closure cap` and `Candidate cap` are **Related parties to
reach** and **Candidates to record**. These are the same stored values under better words, so the
firm's log, the settings screen and the printed report all read the new ones.

**A check no longer asks which trigger to file it under.** Preliminary and comprehensive name _when_
a check ran, not how it searched — the pre-engagement screen, or the moment the firm accepts — and
that is a fact the record already holds. A check filed against a matter the firm has taken on is
comprehensive; every other check is preliminary. The panel says which, rather than asking a member to
classify their own act.

**And a matter is optional, in what the field says as well as in what it accepts.** It always was
accepted without one; the field now says that a matter is where a check is _filed_, not what it is
checked _against_ — naming one adds that matter's own parties and lets the search reach the firm's
own people, and leaving it empty is a real choice rather than an omission.

**A blank number is the firm's own, and now shows which number that is** — inside the box, as its
placeholder, instead of in a block of shorthand at the bottom of the panel.
- **The tasks screen's Done and Cancelled boxes move below the list, and its search and New Task move
into the screen header.** `TaskList` stopped deciding where its own controls sit: it renders the
search, the create control and the clear into a `screenHeader` snippet its host provides, so
`/tasks` seats them in the masthead's action row — the position every other main screen keeps them
in — while a matter's Tasks section, which has no masthead of its own, still draws the row under its
heading. What is closed is asked for at the foot of the list by two controls that name their own
undo, so nothing over the rows competes with the search for the row a reader searches from; the
clear control is now `DataTable.ClearFilters` rather than a seventh hand-rolled funnel, and it
speaks for the search alone, because asking to see done work widens the list rather than narrowing
it. The create control also stops being swapped out for Cancel while the composer is open — it holds
its place in the row, per the design system's own rule, and abandoning a draft is asked for in the
draft.
- **The conflicts screen is the log, and a check is asked for in a panel.** `/conflicts` opened on the
composer: a matter picker, then the whole scope form — parties, sources, band, three edge budgets,
two caps — and only then, below the fold, the list of what the firm had actually run. That put a form
almost nobody was filling in that visit in front of the record almost everybody came for, and it made
the run control something a reader scrolled to rather than reached for.

The screen is now the List archetype it always was: one table at the full width over
`GET /api/v1/conflicts/checks`, cursor-paged with a load-more, and narrowed from its own column
headings — Run, Trigger, Asked By, Against, Band, Floor, Depth (hidden by default) and Candidates.
Running a check is the create act performed over that log: **New Check** at the end of the header's
action row, the design system's one `CreateControl`, opening the product's one `ActionDialog`.

The form did not change; it moved. `check-runner.svelte` became `check-form.svelte` — the fields and
nothing else, handing back the request it composes (or null with the reason it cannot yet) so the
panel owns the commit, the busy state and the failure band. `new-check-dialog.svelte` is that panel,
and it is the same panel from both doors: opened from the firm's log it asks which matter, opened
from a matter it states the matter and asks nothing about it. The matter's own Conflicts section
therefore stopped carrying a second copy of the composer, and its header's New Check now opens the
panel instead of scrolling the reader to a heading.

Two things the register deliberately does not do. It has no Matter column: a check summary carries
the matter's handle and no name, and the matters listing has no read that takes a set of handles, so
the column would be one request per row — what it can say honestly from the summary alone is whether
the search was filed against a matter at all, which is the pre-engagement screen told apart from the
engagement one. And no column is a conclusion: `apps/web/test/conflicts-check-columns.test.ts` pins
that, along with the three-way answer to who asked — a member, `Run automatically`, or a row written
before the trigger source existed, which must not collapse into the second.

**And a check a person asked for now says so on the row.** `POST /api/v1/conflicts/checks` — the
route behind every deliberate run — never set `triggerSource`, so the check was stored with none at
all: the shape of a row written before the column existed. On the old surface that was one muted line
in a list; on a register with an Asked By column it is the column, reading "the row does not say what
started it" beside an actor the same row does in fact name. That is a third and worse claim than
either honest one. The route now passes `triggerSource: "manual"` — which `runConflictsCheck` already
recognized, and which the re-check route beside it has always sent — and
`apps/api-worker/test/conflicts-routes.test.ts` asserts it. Nothing else moves: a null source already
suppressed the announcement, and "manual" suppresses it for the stated reason (the person who asked
is looking at the result).
- **Three corrections from a walk of the deployed app.**

**The calendar makes things with New, like everything else.** The firm calendar's primary action was a hand-built dropdown reading "Record" — the product's one create control, re-implemented under a different verb — and it is `CreateControl` now, reading the bare "New" over "New Event", "New Deadline" and "New Firm Event". The matter's own calendar section had the same mislabel from the other side: it read "New Event" over a menu that also records a deadline. A control that opens a menu reads the bare "New" and the items carry the nouns; the section registry says which sections those are (`CREATE_SEVERAL_KINDS`), so the label does not change under the reader as the page mounts. Each kind wears the glyph it already wears wherever it is named — a calendar, a clock, a building — rather than a second choice made per menu. The gate that refuses a rival create button never walked the calendar's routes, which is how the hand-built one survived; it walks them now.

**The header's controls name themselves on hover.** Notifications, Time Sheet, Downloads, Build Information — one name each, through the design system's Tooltip. Three of the four had no hover text at all and the fourth explained what pressing it would do, so four controls in one band read as four kinds of thing. Where the control is already a popover's trigger the two share one button: `Tooltip.Trigger` now takes bits' `child` snippet, which app code could not reach before because bits-ui is importable only inside the design system.

**The custody register is one table at the full width.** The container tree down its left side is gone. It narrowed to a whole branch — a subtree read no column filter over loaded rows can express — and that did not pay for making this register read as a different kind of table from every other one; Location was already a set-filtered column, narrowed from its own header the way Status is. The server's subtree read stays in the API, and the holdings-by-location report stays with it, for the custody reports.
- The custodian's three panels — logging a packet, describing an item, filing a copy — are the first screens to open in `ActionDialog`.

They landed the same week the shell did, each carrying the scaffold by hand: its own open flag, its own busy flag, its own footer, and no guard on the way out. `lint:one-ui` caught all three the moment the two branches met, which is what the rule is for. They are migrated rather than allowanced: an allowance records debt that predates a rule, and these postdate it.

Being real callers changed the shell twice, which is what first adopters are for. A commit now takes a second word for the same verb — "Logging" beside "Log Packet" — because thirteen panels across the product already changed their label in flight and losing that would have been a visible regression. And the reason a commit is refused is now **rendered** at the weak end of the action bar rather than only hovered: a `title` is not discoverable by anyone who is not already hunting for it, and the reader who most needs it is the one looking at a control that will not press.

All three gain the guard they never had: Escape, the corner dismiss and a press outside now ask before throwing away a half-described will.
- **A firm using this platform cannot record a client's telephone number, and nothing in the schema
says so.** `directory_email`, `directory_phone` and `directory_address` have been in the per-firm
schema since the baseline migration. They are temporal, soft-deleted, indexed, carry an `is_primary`
flag whose enforcement the schema comments describe, and all three are registered for subject
erasure. Twenty-five directory routes, and not one touches any of them. The email table has a write
path built for inbound capture and reachable only from it; phone and address have no domain module
at all, so there is not one statement anywhere in the repository that inserts a telephone number or
an address for a person. The record screen lists seven panes and none of them is Contact.

The design pass that found it is at
[`docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-08-30-directory-entity-model-design.md),
and its first conclusion is that the model is much deeper than the screen suggests, so this is a
completion rather than a rebuild. Names are already temporal, role-typed, phonetically coded and
match-keyed twice over; identifiers are already one sealed row per value with a per-type frozen
normalize transform and an explicit, reasoned blind-index policy. Neither is touched.

What the pass proposes, grounded in RFC 6350, FHIR R4, NIEM's `nc:PersonType`, schema.org, Popolo,
and the professional-conduct rules the data exists to serve: the contact tables reached by an API
and a pane before anything structural changes; a phone split into what technology answers it and in
what context, with a canonical E.164 form beside the number as entered and the extension in its own
column, because fax is a technology and work is a context and one free-text label cannot be both;
identifier types promoted from bare strings to registered scheme descriptors shipped as package
reference data, with the issuing jurisdiction moved out of the sealed value into its own column and
the frozen transform still seeing byte-identical input so no existing blind index is invalidated;
date of birth, date of death and a deceased flag moved onto the person, because a range query over
ciphertext is not a query and `IdentifierNotIndexableError` already exists as the symptom; an
organization given a kind, a jurisdiction of formation and a life, which the schema's own
`court_entity_id` and `estate_entity_id` have needed since they were written; provenance and a
verification status on every contact point and identifier, where `failed` — returned mail, a bounce,
a disconnected line — is the state with nowhere to live today and the one an affidavit of diligence
turns on; a no-contact warning derived per matter from who represents the party rather than stored as
a flag on a person, because Rule 4.2 is scoped to the matter and a stale warning teaches people to
dismiss warnings; and the edge catalog split so a constituent who can bind an organization is
distinguishable from one who cannot, since the conflicts traversal currently spends its control
budget on a mailroom clerk with the same weight it spends on a chief executive.

Nine decision fragments accompany it. Eight open questions are put to the owner rather than settled,
the largest being whether a date of birth sits in plaintext, in plaintext as a birth year beside the
retained sealed date, or unchanged.
- **The Directory's round of owner corrections — the index's columns, and the record panel.**

The index carries twelve columns instead of three. Beside the name and the kind sit the record's
default email address, its default number and the city of its default address; the parts a name was
assembled from (first, middle, last), an organization's legal name, the region and country, and when
the record last changed are declared and start hidden, offered from the header menu's Columns
submenu. The three contact facts are the DEFAULT row per channel — one email, one number, one place,
the row a message goes to when nobody named an address — read for the page in one query rather than
joined into the union the listing walks (`packages/directory/src/entity-listing.ts`). A sealed
identifier is not among them and will not be: reading one is a permission-gated, audited decrypt, and
a page of fifty rows cannot ask that. The filter popover above the table is gone; the Kind column's
own set filter was already doing its whole job, and the way back to the whole book is
`DataTable.ClearFilters` in the header row.

On the record panel: a person is recorded with a first name and nothing more required — a mononym is
an ordinary name, the domain already indexes one from the given name, and the missing last name is
stated as a warning above the commit rather than as a refusal. The name fields read First, Middle and
Last. The prefix and the suffixes moved off free-text inputs onto the product's own honorific
field (`apps/web/src/lib/names/honorific-field.svelte`, which the settings round built the same day),
so a person carries as many suffixes as they hold. The Contact and Identifiers entry rows lost the box around them and are the last row of their
own list; the identifier row wraps instead of running off the right edge of the panel. A recorded
email, number or address can now be corrected in place instead of only deleted and retyped. The
postal address moved out of the Contact kind dropdown onto its own rail section, over a new
`AddressFields` design-system component whose field set, labels and order follow the country
(`packages/design-system/src/lib/components/address-fields/address-format.ts` is the per-country
table; adding a country is one entry). And both panels hold one height for the screen they open on,
so pressing a rail item no longer resizes the panel out from under the reader.
- **The matters docket shows every matter by default and the scope control is gone.** "The working
docket / Open matters / Closed matters / Consultations" duplicated a narrowing the table's own Status
filter already performs, and the owner ruled it out twice.

Removing it needed a read change rather than a deletion: the matters listing omits unnumbered
consultations by default and its status parameter takes one status, never all. So the screen now
reads both streams in parallel, merges them, and carries the two server cursors as one token. Merging
across page boundaries is safe only because the grid sorts what it holds, and that reason is written
where the merge happens — it would not be safe for a surface rendering rows in fetch order. Either
stream failing fails the whole read, because half a docket looks exactly like a small firm.

**Opening a matter is one screen.** Entry on the left across three tabs — the matter, the client, the
people — and Clearance standing permanently on the right: the conflict check with its subjects
derived live from the title and client as they are typed, the consultation fee, and the trust
deposit. Clearance is deliberately not a fourth tab, and the reason is recorded: it is not more data
being entered, it is the gate the entry has to pass, and a gate behind a tab is one somebody has to
remember to go and look at. It fits 1280x720 without scrolling.

**A defect on the screen whose job is saying who carries the matter:** the Responsible Attorney field
showed its ghost text while the seat was filled. It now shows who holds the seat at rest and clears
to the whole roster on focus, and a collecting seat empties after each pick.

The matter's Custodian tab stops reading Soon — the surface is real and the sidebar already said
Alpha. Every other section was audited against its route in the same pass; the ones still marked Soon
are stubs, correctly.
- **The account door asks for an address and a password, and confirming mints the session.** The owner's 2026-09-09 pass over the deployed sign-in surface, recorded in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`.

`register-account-screen.svelte` drops the first and last name fields — `name` is now optional on `POST /api/v1/registrations` and the address is filed as `registration.display_name` where none is given, never a guess split out of the address — and gains a verify-password field gating the submit.

The confirmation handler in `routes/registrations.ts` now hands back a session: it inserts the `user` row unverified and calls Better Auth's own verify-email endpoint with a freshly minted token, under the new `emailVerification.autoSignInAfterVerification`, forwarding that endpoint's `Set-Cookie` onto its own 200. `next` gains a third value, `signedIn`, so the contract snapshot and the generated client move with it. A mint that does not happen flips `email_verified` directly and answers `signIn` — the credential is already committed, so the front door opens first try, and the account is never left in the one state `requireEmailVerification` refuses. Reasoning: `docs/decisions/pending/confirming-a-registration-is-a-sign-in.md`.

Around them: the persistent-session prop is `rememberMe` and reads "Remember Me"; `AuthPanel`'s `backLabel` names the destination rather than prefixing "Back to"; `check-email-screen.svelte` and `confirm-registration-screen.svelte` take that control instead of a foot button and nothing respectively; `reset-password-request-screen.svelte` loses its meta line; and `joining-choice-screen.svelte` loses its `name` prop with the greeting that used it.
- **`apps/magna-carta-edit` is now `apps/edit-worker`.** The directory disagreed with the package
inside it, which has always been `@magna-carta/edit-worker`, and with every sibling's
`<thing>-worker` shape. Renaming it is the whole change: paths updated in the two tsconfig solutions,
the root `vite.config.ts` test project list, the CI gate's test-node package list,
`tooling/lint-test-collection`, the deploy and build-performance runbooks, two `roadmap.d/` evidence
lines, and the cross-references from the worker's editing area and the search worker.

**The deployed Worker keeps the name `magna-carta-edit`** — that is a Cloudflare script name and
renaming it would orphan the deployment. Only the source directory moved. Its Workers Builds **root
directory must be repointed to `apps/edit-worker`**, or the build cannot find the package.

Historical records are left as written: `CHANGELOG.md` and the two 2026-07-01 review documents cite
the old path because that is where the code was when they were written.
- **The editor image no longer switches off `mount_jail_tree`, and the capabilities experiment is recorded as a success.** The owner's deploy of 2026-09-19 showed the runtime jails the kit with `security.capabilities` at its default (the audit reports each document as securely contained), which makes a mount namespace of the kit's own likely, and in that namespace the bind mount the fast path needs is permitted. coolwsd tests the mount at startup and falls back to copying if it fails, so the worst outcome is the audit's "cannot bind-mount" line rather than an outage; the Dockerfile's note carries the one-line revert.
- The document editor's container class no longer carries `max_instances: 10`.

Ten was the number of documents the whole fleet could have open at once, across every firm, and the eleventh open would have failed at the container stage of the staged-open screen with nothing to say why. A fixed per-class cap is a cliff a growing fleet walks off; the bound is now the account's concurrent-instance limit, as it already is for six of the eight container workers here. The Host-label check in `apps/edit-worker/src/document-routing.ts` is what keeps an invented label from booting a container, and it is unchanged.

The size comment beside it is corrected. It named a "custom ~2.5 GiB instance" as the target, which the platform cannot configure — a custom type needs at least 1 vCPU and 3 GiB per vCPU — and it quoted a 1.16 GiB idle floor for which no measurement was ever recorded. The comment now says what is and is not known, and points at the sizing method in `docs/research/2026-09-18-local-first-document-editing.md`.
- **The editor container settles on `standard-1`, and the image switches the server audit off.** After a week of sizes: `standard-4` cleared the audit's hardware warning and felt no different to use, so the owner kept the smallest size on 2026-09-20 and accepted the warning as the stated consequence. The warning counts as an error to the audit, and with `IsAdminUser` true for every member it would put the "Check warnings of your server" snackbar over every open, so `disable_server_audit=true` joins `extra_params`; there is no per-line switch. Taking it out for one deploy brings the audit back for a diagnosis. `docs/operating-costs.md` carries the sizes and what each buys.
- **The editor container is `standard-4` for one round, to see the audit's hardware warning clear.** coolwsd sets that warning whenever the kernel shows it fewer than four threads; `per_document.max_concurrency` cannot clear it, since it is only ever clamped down to the thread count, and the audit's only override (`disable_server_audit`) switches the whole audit off. Four vCPUs is the smallest instance that shows four threads, so this is the experiment; the owner's standing ruling is the `standard-1` price, and the container returns there once the audit is read. `docs/operating-costs.md` carries the figures.
- **While a document is open, the editor is the whole screen.**

The edit screen drew the app's rail, the top bar, and a header naming the document over the editor, and the editor had what was left. The owner's direction is that the editor is the only thing on the screen: the page declares that it declines the shell, the app layout draws no rail and no top bar for it, and the page draws no header. A failure, a withheld file and a format with no editor keep the shell, because each of those is a message that needs its way back around it. What a member does on the platform from inside the document — save and close, the way back to the matter — will be the editor's own controls, added to its toolbar through its message protocol; until then, the way back is the browser's.
- **The editor image no longer switches off `security.capabilities`.** An experiment the owner asked for on 2026-09-19 to clear the server audit's "Documents are not effectively contained" line: with the setting at its default, coolwsd first tries a user and mount namespace for the kit, and failing that needs the file capabilities the image sets on coolforkit. The Dockerfile's note carries the two outcomes to read after the deploy and the one-line revert (`--o:security.capabilities=false` back into `extra_params`) if no document opens.
- **The editor's corner no longer carries its vendor's logo.**

The editor hides its logo when a hidden field on its page reads `none`, and the community build of the image leaves that field empty with no setting to fill it. The worker in front of the container now fills it, rewriting that one attribute as the page streams through; nothing is injected, because the page's own policy allows no inline style or script, and an upgrade is handed back untouched as before.
- **The editor worker reports its failures through the standard pipeline, and the scrubber recognises a bearer token.**

`magna-carta-edit` had no error boundary. A throw anywhere on the path between the browser and a document's container reached the runtime unhandled: a bare error page, no Error ID, no structured event, and nothing to correlate but a raw exception line in Workers Logs. A WebSocket the container declined was worse — it was silent, because the browser reports every failed handshake as "closed before the connection is established" whatever the server answered, so a container answering 502 and a worker throwing mid-proxy read identically from outside. That is the defect [#633](https://github.com/Phauks/magna-carta/pull/633) fixed, and it took a round trip of guesswork to name; the boundary added here (`apps/edit-worker/src/diagnostics.ts`) would have named it in one log line.

A thrown fault is now a 500 carrying `X-MC-Error-Id` and one `error.captured`; an upgrade the container did not accept is passed through as answered and recorded as one `operation.failed` naming the status — the only record of that status anywhere. The route logged is always the pathname, never the URL: every request the browser makes to this worker carries the WOPI access token as a query parameter, so a quoted URL is a quoted credential. The worker gains the `TELEMETRY` binding the app worker already carries, against the same dataset.

The scrubbing backstop in `@magna-carta/telemetry` now recognises a bearer token in both shapes it travels in — `access_token=…` as written on the wire, and the bare three-segment base64url token an error message carries once something has unpacked the URL. It covered emails, identifiers, cards and phone numbers, and not the one credential this surface puts in every URL.

**A fleet-wide gap, recorded rather than fixed here.** `createWorkersLogger` is used by the app worker and, now, the editor worker. The other five extracted workers — scan, convert, search, OCR, discovery — carry no boundary of this kind either, so golden rule 4 holds for the request path and the WOPI host and not for the Containers fleet. Each wants the same ~60 lines; none is done in this change, because each fronts a different engine whose declining answers mean different things.
- **The event form is four tabs, a staff member is an owner, and a zone reads as one line.** The
owner's round of 2026-09-18 on `apps/web/src/lib/calendar`. `record-event-dialog.svelte` renders
Details, When, Where and Who over `EVENT_FORM_TABS` in `event-draft.ts`; its Belongs to is the
product's one closed-choice field with three owners, and the staff arm is `withMemberListed` — a
firm event with the people-listed audience and that member first. The second field on that line is
one slot, so the choice no longer reflows the form. `readsAsAllDay` / `asAllDay` are the All Day
switch's reading. The design system's `inAllDayBand` (`day-axis.ts`) sends a run of days to the
band above the hours; `day-segments.ts` no longer cuts a span into per-day pieces, which is what
drew a trial across every hour and gave each piece an id no press could open. `formatTimeZone` and
`describeTimeZone` join the display vocabulary (`formatters/instant.ts`) as the one line every zone
reads as, on the record's day; `time-zone-options.ts` orders the rest west to east and searches a
haystack, and `formatWallClock` prints the code beside an hour. `location-picker.svelte` offers the
offices with their addresses (the calendar context reads `listOffices` whole), the rooms, and the
directory's organizations through `directoryPickerSearch`. `participantsBySource` bundles the
chips. `calendar-menu.svelte` is the rail's selection as a dropdown, drawn by `CalendarView` on
`calendarMenu` for the day pane. Every self-clearing picker passes `allowDeselect={false}`, which
is what emptied the matter field on a re-pick. `DISCARD_SENTENCE` is gone from the action dialog.
The design system's `Tooltip.Provider` defaults `ignoreNonKeyboardFocus` on, so the focus a
closing popover hands back to the header's button no longer opens its tooltip.
- **The fee arrangement moves from the Fees screen into the matter status window, and a version can name its signed agreement.** `matter-status-dialog.svelte` reads the arrangement on open and shows an Engagement section (agreement on file, billed as, terms, in force since, folded history) with Amend seated beside it; `fee-ledger.svelte` and `fee-details-panel.svelte` lose the strip, View and Amend, and `arrangement-dialog.svelte` is deleted with its allowance. `matter_billing_arrangement` gains a nullable `agreement_file_id` (a matter file, the conflicts waiver's precedent), carried through `setBillingArrangement`, the route contract and the client; the amend dialog gains a document picker, now the shared `matter-document-picker.svelte`.
- **The file icon resolves from the name first; the type-mismatch finding grades in the icon's own
vocabulary.** `resolveFileCategory` in the design system's file-icon module reads the extension
before the sniffed content type, and an unrecognized extension resolves to `unknown` rather than
falling through to the bytes. A bytes-first sibling, `resolveFileContentCategory`, serves handling
decisions (`editable-documents.ts` keeps opening a Word document renamed `.txt` in the Word editor).
`file-analysis.ts` drops its ten-entry extension-to-MIME list and compares `claimedFileCategory`
against `sniffedFileCategory` at the level of kind: an unrecognized extension over a read sniff is a
mismatch, no extension is no claim, a sniff with no known kind is no reading. Rulings round R25.
- The file list's File Type column shows the file's real extension — "pdf", "docx", "mp4" — instead of a category word we invented for it ("Word", "Video", "Archive"). The extension is what the file actually is; the category was our paraphrase, and the owner ruled the paraphrase out of the file manager. A file whose name carries no extension falls back to the extension its sniffed media type implies, and when nothing is known the cell is blank rather than a placeholder phrase like "Not known yet". Sorting the column follows what it shows, with blank cells sorting after every known type.
- Five more panels open in `ActionDialog`: the ones the four directory panes compose.

The panes had been excluded from the migration as "panes inside a surface, not modals," a reason that described the files rather than the hits; each pane holds a real form dialog. Assign A Category, Record A Way To Reach Them, Record An Identifier, Change The Name On The Record and Record Another Name are now on the shell, on `LabelledField` and `FieldRow` where they had hand-minted ids, each refusing its commit with a reason where it used to disable silently, and each asking before a stray Escape throws typed work away (the change dialog compares against the name it was seeded with, so an untouched seed asks nothing).

Four allowances leave the registry; six remain, every one a named exclusion. The design records the correction: an allowance's reason should name the panel it excuses, not the file that holds it.
- **`apps/worker` is now `apps/api-worker`, and `@magna-carta/worker` is `@magna-carta/api-worker`.**

Thirteen of the fourteen entries under `apps/` name the Worker they hold — `scan-worker`,
`sign-worker`, `status-worker`. One was called `worker`, which said only that it was one of them, and
it happened to be the largest: the API Worker carrying D1, R2, Queues, Durable Objects, the
WebAssembly modules and every runtime secret. A reader arriving at `apps/worker` had to open it to
learn which Worker it was.

Directory and package rename only. **The Cloudflare script name is unchanged** (`magna-carta`), so
nothing in production moves and no Durable Object namespace is affected — but the Workers Builds
dashboard root directory for that project must be repointed to `apps/api-worker` or its next build
cannot find the package. That step is in `docs/deploy-queue.md`.

`apps/web` is left where it is. It is the SvelteKit application, not a Worker, and `apps/web-worker`
is already taken by the assets-only deployable that serves its build output — the two are separate
packages on purpose, and the one that produces the bytes is a dependency of the one that serves them.

`docs/specs`, `docs/decisions`, `docs/research` and the rendered `CHANGELOG.md` keep the old path:
they record what was true when they were written.
- Four more panels open in `ActionDialog`, and two of them are the first callers of the seams the shell just gained.

Move to Another Ledger hands the shell `commitSoon` with the dependency the move waits on, so the shell wraps its own commit in the Soon affordance and the panel no longer composes one around a commit of its own. New Person / New Organization lays its fields out with `LabelledField` and `FieldRow`, which mint the ids and wire the labels; its "Checking the firm's record" hint moves from the bar into the body. Fold One Record Into The Other is a `destructive` kind — the alertdialog role, no incidental dismiss, the commit in the colour of an act that takes something away — and states why its commit is refused until the acknowledgement is ticked, where it used to be silently disabled. Answer This Hit puts its rationale and the waiver's pickers in labelled fields and its "recorded as a new row" line in the body.

Four allowances leave the registry; fifteen remain, eleven of them named exclusions. Two wording changes: "Record the answer" is "Record the Answer", and the commit icons (the arrows, the merge glyph) are gone, as they went from billing.
- Filling the screen is the frame's, not one shell's.

The record window's expand — the corner control, the session memory, the geometry that drops the width cap — moves beneath both modal shells as `internal/frame-expansion.svelte.ts`, and `ActionDialog` gains the same control on its Dialog kinds (`form`, `reading`; never on a question) with its own session memory, kept apart from the record window's: a reader who filled the screen with one form has said nothing about the next question they are asked. Both shells take a bindable `expanded`, which is how a panel opens expanded by design. The record window's four frame-bearing stories are byte-identical before and after.

The one panel that had rebuilt all of this by hand — the time sheet's own flag, icons and utilities inside a raw dialog — migrates with the other two full-screen surfaces in the pass that follows.
- **The whole-repo quality gate is `pnpm gate`, run on the machine that made the change, and the GitHub
Actions workflow that used to be it is gone.** The account's Actions minutes ran out on 2026-08-05,
again on 2026-09-03, and each time the required `gate` status stopped reporting: every pull request
wedged behind a check that had not run and merged on an administrator override, so the gate failed
closed on the budget and open on the code. `tooling/gate/index.mjs` now runs the same dimensions from
one command — format, governance, the pinned osv-scanner audit over both supply chains, the WASM
artefacts, the type-check, the four contract-drift checks, the type-aware lint over the affected
closure (sinks included, nothing deferred), the Rust and container gates where the change reaches
them, the test-collection floor and the full `pnpm test` — with the workflow's own path classification
deciding which have an input, `--plan` printing the decision, and a summary block the pull-request
template now asks for in place of the label. `gate.yml`, `seed-caches.yml` and `lint:cache-keys` are
deleted; `assemble-docs.yml` no longer dispatches a gate onto its assembly branch;
`lint:test-collection` keeps its collection floor and drops the partition proof that only a sharded
split needed; `lint:lints` reads the fitness-sweep step off the gate's own step list instead of YAML;
`lint:affected-scope` drops its verbatim-invocation check because the gate calls the classifier
directly. One owner step remains and is on the deploy queue: remove `gate` from the `main` ruleset's
required status checks, or GitHub keeps waiting for a check nothing will report.
- **The gate runs the test substrates a change can reach, restores its WASM artefacts from `main`, and is sectioned by tier.** The first month of real gate runs showed where the bill goes: `test-worker` (two to four 2-core shards of eight to ten minutes each) was the largest single item on every pull request, and every branch's first run paid a ~7-minute cold Docker build of the WASM packages because nothing had saved that cache on `main` since the push-to-main tier was suspended — a pull request can only restore what its own branch or `main` saved.

Three changes in `.github/workflows/gate.yml` and beside it:

- **Substrate gating.** `classify` (the job formerly called `changes`) now emits whether the Miniflare suites (`apps/api-worker`, `apps/status-worker`) and the Storybook suite (`packages/design-system`) are reachable from the change, read off the same undeferred dependent closure the lint scope already uses; `test-worker` and `test-stories` are skipped when they are not. A UI-only change never boots a Workers runtime and an api-only change never boots Chromium. The reading is fail-safe: `ALL` and `NONE` (a crate, a container, a workflow) both run everything, and only a concrete package list that omits the substrate's package skips it. `lint` is likewise skipped at the job level on a `NONE` scope instead of paying a 2-core runner to print that.
- **`seed-caches.yml`.** On every push to `main`, restore-or-build the WASM artefacts under the gate's own cache key, so a branch's first run hits. `pnpm run lint:cache-keys` (`tooling/lint-cache-keys`) holds the two key expressions identical, because a seed under a different key warms nothing.
- **Named and sectioned.** Jobs are grouped under banners by tier — classify, always-on guards, WASM artefacts, consumers, Rust and containers, aggregate — and named for what they do (`classify`, `build-wasm`). The four-step preamble every consumer repeated (checkout, setup, download the artefact, untar it) is now `./.github/actions/setup` with `wasm: "true"`, so each job's steps are what that job checks.

`assemble-docs.yml` moves to the 1-vCPU runner and installs the workspace only once the dependency-free assemblers have produced something to format; its second run per merge, which finds nothing, now costs a checkout. Standard: `docs/conventions/build-performance.md`.

One gate-reliability fix rides along: the worker suites' `beforeAll` hooks apply the control-plane migrations and, in the heavier files, seed several firms through the real registration flow, which on a loaded 2-core runner overran Vitest's 10-second default twice in one afternoon while every test in the file would have passed. `apps/api-worker/vitest.config.ts` sizes `hookTimeout` to that work; the per-test timeout is unchanged.
- **Five user guides caught up with where the file tools actually are.** Four told the reader to open the Tools sidebar and pick a standalone tool that is now a File Workbench tab (Hash, Metadata, Unlock), and the workbench's own guide still routed through Tools rather than the sidebar. A guide that sends somebody to a screen that no longer exists is worse than no guide.

`attorney-license-lookup.md` is new, and carries the two things the screen cannot say at length: why Magna Carta sends you to the state's register rather than answering for you (standing is exactly the fact that changes after you look, so a stale copy would be worse than none), and what an unencrypted register means for the name you are about to type into it.
- The handover told the next instance to verify in a browser and left out the recipe, which is not guessable: two remote-only wrangler bindings have to be commented out before the worker boots, the dev seed returns the credentials, and a Playwright run has to POST those to the sign-in endpoint on the page's own request context before any `(app)` route is reachable. It now carries all of that, plus the instruction to measure rather than eyeball — a `boundingBox()` on the thing you changed, and a walk up the ancestor chain when a flex child will not stretch.

The count of render-only defects in that section went from three to five: the two that shipped to `main` past a green gate, fifteen passing tests and a clean build are the strongest argument the section makes.
- **Three harness defects that all punished the honest path: retiring a stream note left a dangling
pointer, ending a test run left the runners alive, and a docs-only diff had to build three Rust
crates to be gated. All measured, all now one command or one condition.**

**Retiring an active-work note is one operation — `vp run retire-note <branch>`.** The worktree
lifecycle read as three parts (remove the worktree, delete the branch, delete
`docs/active-work/<branch>.md`) and had a fourth nobody had written down: any `status.d/` fragment
carrying `active-work: docs/active-work/<branch>.md` is then dangling, and `pnpm run lint:status`
fails with "active-work points at a missing file". It bit five times in one session — twice caught by
the lint after the fact, twice pre-empted by remembering to grep, once missed again by somebody who
already knew. The fourth part is invisible from where the deletion happens: nothing in
`docs/active-work/` knows who references it. So the command clears every pointer naming the note,
re-renders `STATUS.md`/`STATUS.json`, deletes the note, and removes the worktree and branch — the
pointer cannot outlive the note because the same command removes both. It refuses a branch that has
not landed (`--force` overrides, `--dry-run` previews, `--keep-workspace` does the paperwork only),
and it runs `lint:status` itself before reporting success. `vp run worktrees` already knew which
notes were dead; it now names each one's dependent fragments and this command in the same breath, and
the lint's own failure line names the repair instead of offering generic advice that cannot fix it.

**Ending a test run now ends the runners.** `pnpm test` killed its direct child, which is `vp` — two
levels above the work. Under it sit the Vitest CLI, the esbuild services and the workerd instances the
Miniflare suites stand up; signalling only `vp` orphans the rest. Measured interrupting
`pnpm test apps/api-worker`: the guard exited after 17 s and **released the single-flight lock with nine
runner processes still alive**, which stayed up a further **44 s**. The next run then claims the lock
correctly — its holder really has gone — and starts into a machine that is not idle, which is the
contention the lock exists to prevent arriving through the one door it does not watch, and which
presents as timeouts in files neither run touched. The runner now leads its own process group;
teardown is SIGTERM, a grace window, SIGKILL for the remainder, and the lock is released only once
the group is confirmed empty. The wait is bounded — a survivor is reported and the lock freed anyway,
because a lock held until an unkillable runner dies is the 0%-CPU holder the guard exists to
eliminate. Same target after: **zero survivors**. Detaching is gated on stdin not being a terminal,
which is the exact shape of the `SIGTTIN` hazard that would otherwise wedge `vp test --watch`, and
where the gate declines the kernel already signals the whole foreground group on Ctrl-C.

**A docs-only diff no longer has to bootstrap.** `check:scoped` ran its type-check unconditionally,
and `tsc -b` builds the whole project-reference graph — so the generated wasm artefacts were needed
whatever the diff was, and a branch touching only `docs/` and the ledger fragments had to build three
Rust crates (~80–100 s cold) before a gate that would not read a line of its own diff. The response
that produced was `git push --no-verify`, which is the real cost: a gate that makes bypassing it the
rational choice trains people to bypass it. The type-check is now scoped like every other conditional
step, and the artefact prerequisite scopes with it — skipping the artefact check _alone_ would have
been the bug, trading one message that names its own repair for twelve `TS2307`s that do not.
`tooling/check-scoped/typecheck-scope.mjs` enumerates what provably cannot be an input to `tsc -b`
(prose anywhere, the `docs/` tree, the rendered `STATUS.json`) and runs the check unless every changed
path is one of those, so a new extension or directory nobody anticipated takes the check. Measured in
a fresh, un-bootstrapped worktree: a docs-only diff passes in **2.4 s**; adding one `.ts` file to the
same diff correctly demands the artefacts and then type-checks, naming the path that made it run.
- Round eight of the matter file manager. Every icon on the screen is now Lucide geometry taken straight from the installed package rather than hand-drawn path data — the owner's standing rule, now true of the mockup and binding on the build. Colour and Icon are two separate right-click items instead of one nested inside the other; the palette runs in rainbow order, gained pink, and its swatches are actually square (`.menu button` sets a corner radius and outranked a bare `.swatch`, which is why two earlier rounds of "make them square" changed nothing visible).

Both side panels now resize by dragging their inner edge, identically, with arrow keys and a double-click reset. Document type is a dropdown anchored to whatever opened it rather than a modal that blanks the screen. Tab strips scroll sideways only. The list runs to the edge of its column, and a column's filter control sits with that column's label and reserves its space so revealing it moves nothing.

File Analysis counts by severity rather than by how many files have anything at all; an issue can be ignored, the ignored ones reviewed, and any of them taken back; Safety History opens the panel it points at, which it previously did not; and the whole set of findings can be copied or downloaded. A scanner finding can be copied or downloaded too, both rendered from one text so they cannot disagree.

Deleted files are matter files, so they render on the matter's own table — same columns, same sorting, same right-click, same multiple selection — plus Deleted, Deleted By and Was In. Sorting by deletion time is what that list is for.
- **Design proposed for moving the single-page application onto its own Worker**, so an interface change
stops rebuilding and redeploying the API:
[`docs/specs/2026-08-21-spa-worker-split-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-08-21-spa-worker-split-design.md).
Design only, and gated on a measurement — two reversible settings on the existing Worker may close
most of the gap first, in which case the proposal should be withdrawn rather than built.

**Corrects a claim in [`operations.md`](docs/conventions/operations.md) that had stood since
2026-06-28:** that `@magna-carta/pdf` is "imported by the SPA". It is not. `apps/web` depends on none
of the three WebAssembly packages; every importer of the pdf package is server-side. The sentence
mattered because it is why "can the interface build without the Rust toolchain?" carried an answer of
no for two months without anyone reading the dependency graph.

Also recorded there: the assets binding declares `run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]` while the Worker also
serves `/wopi/*` and `/search-objects/*`, so by the configuration as written a public request to
either would be answered by the single-page-application fallback rather than by its handler. Whether
that is reachable depends on service-binding behaviour this repository has not tested, so it is filed
as a finding rather than a fix. The split would make it moot; without the split the repair is to add
both prefixes.
- **The interface ships on its own Worker: the app's hostname is split by route pattern, and a UI
merge no longer has any reason to rebuild the API.**

The 2026-08-21 split design's two owner flags were answered and the cutover performed
(2026-08-31): the custom domain on `magna-carta` became route patterns on the zone —
`magna-carta-web` serves every path, `magna-carta` only `/api/*`, `/wopi/*`, `/search-objects/*`
and `/__dev/*`. Same origin, same cookie, no CORS; nothing auth-side moved. The decision, the one
deliberate departure from the design (the API Worker keeps its `assets` block as the local-dev
vehicle and one-gesture rollback — `wrangler dev` and the e2e suite serve the whole app from it),
and the accepted deploy-skew cost are recorded in the `the-interface-ships-on-its-own-worker` ADR.

In the repository, the change is mostly the record and one honest retirement: the version
overlay's page-versus-API "Different Builds" warning described a normal state once the two deploy
separately, so it is gone — the overlay's topology line explains why the rows may differ, and the
version poll's Update Available notice remains the one reload signal. The final decoupling lever
is dashboard state (dropping `apps/web/*` from the `magna-carta` project's Build Watch Paths) and
is tracked on the deploy queue.
- Add a Document opens in `ActionDialog`, and with it every panel in the migration's scope is on one of the two shells.

Its two paths — from a file, from a template — share the shell's one commit, whose verb follows the open path ("Add Document", "Build Document") and refuses with the reason until that path has what it needs. A document that landed, whether created, rejected by the scan, or still being checked, leaves the panel `done` with the outcome in place of the form; a request that never reached the server, or a problem the server stated, is a refusal with the reason in the notice band and the form still in hand.

Apply Trust Funds, excluded while the Soon affordance lived in the app, is a plain form with `commitSoon` now that the shell carries the affordance; its dependency reads on the commit's hover and to a screen reader rather than as a line beneath it.

Twenty-seven panels migrated across six pull requests. Ten `hand-composed-modal` allowances remain in `tooling/lint-one-ui/registry.json`, every one a named exclusion: the command palette (a launcher), the four directory panes (panes, not modals), the settings ledger (a Sheet), the three full-screen surfaces (a separate design), and the fee-arrangement window (`RecordWindow`'s shape).
- **Twenty-eight areas of the feature ledger were read against the repository, and the drift ran almost
entirely in one direction: nodes describing work that has since landed.** The staleness gate keys on a
node NAMING a code path, or carrying a `slices:` tag whose fragment reports built. Of 755 nodes, 162
assert an absence in prose while naming no path, and 133 of those carry no slice tag either — outside
every rule by construction. That is roughly a fifth of the ledger the gate is structurally unable to
read, and it was green over all of it.

**The largest correction is Custodian, where three nodes describe work slice 4·2·4 shipped.**
Stocktake sits at `deferred` saying the MVP ships container data with no stocktake workflow;
`packages/custodian` carries `stocktake-service`, `stocktake-statements` and `stocktake-reconciliation`
over two tables, with seven routes and a source-scan fitness function holding the observe-only
boundary. Retention-and-destruction sits at `designed` saying `custody_destruction_request` has no
service, no route and nothing that writes it; there are five routes, a service, and database triggers
forcing the requester and approver to differ. Will reminders sits at `deferred` saying the per-state
statute catalog is out of the MVP; the catalog is built with Nevada and two of its counties encoded,
and it is the REMINDER half that is blocked, because the register records no date of death. The area
root counted twenty-five routes over eleven tables against thirty-eight over thirteen.

**Two sibling contradictions, both the shape the discovery sweep found.** Conflicts' strictness node
said Beider-Morse runs at the over-inclusive band while its matching-engine node said Beider-Morse is
unbuilt and gave the workerd measurement for why — the second is right, and what actually widens is
the Double Metaphone scheme filter. Notifications' digest node sits at `deferred` calling the rollup a
declared seam, three blocks below the email node describing the same digest as shipped with its
module, its renderer and its hourly pass.

**Six dependency claims were inverted** — a node saying its dependency is not built where the
dependency ships. `containers/libreoffice` is a Rust supervisor over a pool of office-suite child
processes, so the office conversion engine, the platform's container list, and the document-automation
PDF arm were all describing a gap that closed. `crates/search-core` is Tantivy 0.26, so the Rust-core
node's "Tantivy search not started" and the container node's "Tantivy container not started" were both
wrong. Per-type matter templates said document automation is "Not started" where it is built through
2·6·5. Locations now carries an IANA `time_zone` column, validated on write, which two areas asserted
did not exist.

**And a systematic one the gate cannot see: sixteen nodes across six areas cited `changelog.d/*.md`
fragments as evidence, and every fragment named had been consumed by the assembler.** Every one of
those paths dangled. They are replaced with the code they stood in for, which is more useful anyway —
the settings permission check turns out to be a stated mock returning true for the billing area alone,
which no changelog line was going to say.

**No `status:` value was changed.** The sweep corrects `evidence:` and `notes:` only, on the ground
that restatusing a node one has only read is a claim reading cannot settle. Where a status is
demonstrably behind its own code, the node now says so in its own prose and the register renders the
contradiction rather than hiding it.

**Two shape findings about the gate itself.** Rule 1 (unaccounted code) is disarmed inside any area
whose root names its whole package: a `partial` root naming `packages/custodian` accounts for every
path under it, so a `deferred` child naming a shipped module in the same package never fires. And the
path parser reads a SvelteKit route group out of a path — `apps/web/src/routes/(app)/tools/whois-lookup`
resolves as `tools/whois-lookup` and reports missing — so evidence for a web route has to be written
around it.
- The matter's section strip is grouped, the header's overflow (`...`) control and the Other section
are gone, and Magnus takes a section.

The control held exactly one item — the status's lifecycle action, shipped disabled and marked Soon
— so a member had to open it to discover there was nothing in it to press. That is a control's width
of chrome returning nothing, and it also quietly broke the standing rule it was built to honour: a
designed-but-unwired capability ships VISIBLE, and a seam in a drawer is not visible. The lifecycle
action comes back as a named control on the row when it is wired. Until then the band carries no
actions at all, and its inline-end column is the section strip and nothing else.

The Other section leaves both the registry and the route tree. It was the only tab whose label named
no place: it stood for whatever the other thirteen
did not cover, which is a bin rather than a destination, and its stub had to be written in the
abstract because nothing concrete was ever going to land there first. Content with no home yet waits
for the section that will own it.

In its place, **Magnus gets a matter section** — a `soon` stub for now, at the head of the non-core
group so it is visible on a wide canvas and the last of that group to fold. The assistant reads a
matter rather than recording anything on it, so it does not hold a core record section's width; it
now has both of the homes it was always going to need, the always-reachable sidebar destination and
the conversation already scoped to one matter.

**The strip stopped folding by measurement and started grouping by meaning.** Fourteen sections fit
no canvas: at 1440 the measured fold left seven on the row and put the other seven behind More, and
which seven was decided by pixel arithmetic — Trust and Calendar were buried for sitting late in a
list, not for being less used. The row now carries seven entries, five of them sections and two
named neighbourhoods that open a menu:

**Overview · Files · Money ⌄ · Parties · Calendar · Record ⌄ · Magnus**

Money is Time, Fees, Costs, Billing and Trust; Record is Notes, Emails, Messaging and Custodian.
Only what a member can afford to reach through a menu is grouped: a matter's dates are checked too
often for that, so Calendar stays on the row and Parties with it. The arrangement's order is also
the fold order, so the tail is the cheapest thing to reach through a menu — Magnus, then Record,
then the dates and the people, with Money holding the row longest because all five of its sections
are live.

Measured after building, all seven hold the row at 1440. The measured fold stays underneath as a
backstop for anything narrower, and an entry that reaches it folds as a GROUP — its name becomes a
menu heading over its own sections, so the two routes to one destination never disagree about what
it belongs to.

`sections.ts` now carries two lists with one home: every section that exists, and the arrangement
the strip reads them in, declared by slug. A section nobody placed, a slug naming no section, a
section placed twice, and a group of one are all module-load failures, so the strip cannot silently
stop offering a section that exists. The `core` flag is gone with the flat strip that used it.

All three generalizations are in `docs/conventions/design-corrections.md`, and the Record Detail
archetype carries the grouping rule and no longer lists a `⋯` in its header.
- The matter's section tabs move into the empty half of its header, and the Alpha pillboxes come off the product.

A matter spent two rows before any content: the masthead, whose inline-end half carried one overflow control and otherwise nothing, and then the section strip on a row of its own. Those are now one band. The actions sit on the title's row, the strip sits beneath them packed to the same end, and both share the band's bottom rule — so the gold active bar still lands on a rule rather than floating. The masthead keeps everything it had: the serif title at masthead scale, the ledger line, the citation. 152px of chrome becomes 111px.

Four arrangements were built and measured before this one was chosen, which is the only reason it holds up. An even split of the band was measured against a capped identity block and both against a wrapping one: wrapping the title at a 1024 canvas costs 27px, turning a 42px saving into a net loss, and capping the identity block starved the strip to a single tab. The shipped split truncates the title and the citation instead, so the band is 111px at 1600 and 111px at 1024 rather than growing as the window narrows. The citation became one joined string in the same change, because a flex row of separate entries cannot ellipsis and truncating each entry to its share gives four stubs and no citation.

Separately, `alpha` and `beta` stopped rendering a maturity mark anywhere — the matter tabs, the sidebar destinations, the tools listing, the contacts sections. A surface a member can open does not announce how finished it is, and the pill cost each tab about as much width as its own label. `soon` still marks, because it says there is nothing behind this yet. The stages are unchanged and still decide whether a destination is a live link or a stub.
- The matter's header band goes from 111px to 76px, and `Masthead.Root` learns a `density`.

The section strip already shared the band. What was left was the identity block, which spent three rows on itself: the ledger line, the title, the citation. Now it spends two — the matter number and its status seal lead the citation rather than holding a row above the title — and the title takes the Masthead recipe's new `compact` density, 2rem down to 1.5rem. The step lives in the recipe because the masthead is the one door to the display serif, and a screen that can set `text-2xl` on the Title has taken that door off its hinges.

The change that actually moved the number was on the other side. Six settings were measured, and three that look nothing alike came out at exactly 90px: the inline-end column was the overflow control stacked over the strip — 40px + 8px + 41px = 89px — and it floored the band however short the identity got. Putting the whole identity on one line bought nothing at all. Moving the control onto the strip's own row makes that column 41px, and the identity block sets the height again.

152px of matter chrome at the start of this work, 111px after the strip moved off its own row, 76px now, at every canvas width. A third density step was built, measured and dropped: at 1.25rem the display face is close enough to the citation that the register's scale contrast nearly goes, and it bought nothing over the structural saving.
- **A migration lineage now defends its own apply order, its own bundle and its own history — three tools, all running on every pull request.** Apply order is by TAG, and a branch cut before another one lands keeps its earlier timestamp while drizzle renumbers its `idx` to the end. A fresh database then applies it before the migration it was written on top of, building its schema in an order no existing firm ever used. Nothing about the merge looks wrong afterwards and every firm that already exists keeps working, which is why two of them reached `main` in September 2026.

**The worker's tag-to-SQL bundle is generated from the journal** (`tooling/migration-bundles`). `apps/api-worker/src/per-firm-migrations.ts` and its control-plane sibling were a hand-kept map of forty lines that had to gain an entry every time the journal did, and it lost one three times — a merge resolves the journal cleanly, because its entries are adjacent lines, and drops one branch's import in the same conflict. `migrationsFromJournal` throws on that, but only inside a Durable Object on wake, so it surfaced as a twenty-second route timeout rather than as a missing import. `pnpm run lint:migration-bundles` now fails when a module and its journal disagree. The emitted text is a fixed point of the repo formatter, so the generator and `vp check --fix` cannot undo each other.

**A conflicted `_journal.json` is resolved by a command** (`node tooling/resolve-journal/index.mjs`), not by hand. What decides the answer is not "ours" and "theirs" — which of those is the branch depends on which direction the merge ran — it is `main`, which is production here, so a tag on `main` has deployed and is immutable and a tag that is not can still move for free. Trunk entries keep their tags and their order; everything else is appended in the order it was integrated and re-stamped above the head, its `.sql` renamed to match and the bundles regenerated. It reads git's conflict stages during a merge and the journal on disk otherwise, so it repairs an inversion that already landed as readily as it resolves a live one. `timestamp-latest-migration.mjs` shares its tag arithmetic: two implementations of "a tag that sorts above the head" is the shape of the bug both exist to prevent.

**A migration that has deployed can no longer be changed** (`pnpm run lint:migration-immutability`).
